marks: The hard hat was invented in 1919 by Edward W. Bullard, who had just returned from World War I.
Over the past century, hard hats have improved considerably, moving from canvas and leather to aluminum, fiberglass, and, eventually, thermoplastic.

paras: A hard hat is a helmet worn mainly at worksites to protect the head from injuries caused by falling objects. __31__

The hard hat was invented in 1919 by Edward W. Bullard, who had just returned from World War I. Before the war, workers used to smear their hats with tar to protect their heads. __32__ The result was the Hard Boiled Hat, which was cheap enough for every worker and light enough to wear all day long. Made of steamed canvas and glue, with a leather brim and a coat of black paint, it also had a suspension system inside to soften blows. Hard hats soon came into wide use, and they were later required on major construction projects such as the Hoover Dam in 1931 and the Golden Gate Bridge in 1933.

Over the past century, hard hats have improved considerably, moving from canvas and leather to aluminum, fiberglass, and, eventually, thermoplastic. __33__ A ventilated hard hat, for example, keeps its wearer cooler, while a see-through face shield protects the face without blocking the view. Today, available attachments include radios, sensors, cameras, and much more.

__34__ Yellow is usually worn by general laborers and contractors, white (or sometimes black) by supervisors and managers, and green by inspectors and new workers. No law sets these colors, though, so they can vary from company to company and site to site.

New products continue to expand the market for hard hats. Yet from Bullard’s canvas hat to today’s models fitted with sensors and cameras, the hard hat’s main job has never changed: keeping workers’ heads safe.
zhTranslation: 安全帽是一種主要在工地配戴的頭盔，用來保護頭部，避免被掉落物砸傷。__31__

安全帽是 Edward W. Bullard 在 1919 年發明的，他當時剛從第一次世界大戰返鄉。大戰以前，工人習慣在帽子上塗焦油來保護頭部。__32__ 成果就是 Hard Boiled Hat：價錢便宜到每個工人都買得起，重量也輕到可以整天戴著。這種帽子用蒸過的帆布和膠製成，帽簷是皮革，外面塗上一層黑漆，裡面還裝了懸吊系統來減輕撞擊。安全帽不久就普及開來，後來在大型工程裡更規定一定要戴，例如 1931 年的胡佛水壩和 1933 年的金門大橋。
過去 100 年來，安全帽有了長足的進步，材質從帆布和皮革，換成鋁、玻璃纖維，最後是熱塑性塑膠。__33__ 例如，透氣的安全帽讓配戴的人比較涼爽，透明面罩則能保護臉部，又不會擋住視線。如今可以加裝的配件，還有無線電、感測器、攝影機等等。
__34__ 一般工人和承包商通常戴黃色，監工和經理戴白色（有時是黑色），檢查人員和新進工人則戴綠色。不過，這些顏色並沒有法律規定，所以各公司、各工地的標示方式可能不一樣。
新產品持續擴大安全帽的市場。然而，從 Bullard 的帆布帽，到今天裝上感測器和攝影機的款式，安全帽最主要的任務始終沒有改變：保護工人的頭部。

marks: That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so frightening.
Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it?
Diseases like West Nile thus have as much to do with what officials fail to do as with climate.
paras: West Nile is a viral disease that begins in birds, which pass it on to mosquitoes that then go on to infect human beings with a bite. Most people who contract West Nile never develop any symptoms. In those who do, symptoms appear 2 to 14 days after the bite. About one in five infected people develops a fever, headaches, and body aches, usually lasting a week or so. A far less lucky one in 150 suffers high fever, tremors, paralysis, and coma. __31__

That is what made the major outbreaks of West Nile in the U.S. in the summer of 2012 so frightening. The situation was particularly bad in and around Dallas, Texas, where the virus sickened nearly 400 people and killed 19 that year. __32__ Some residents objected, fearing that the cure could be worse than the disease.

Why was the summer of 2012 so hospitable to the West Nile virus and the mosquitoes that carry it? __33__ An extremely mild winter allowed more mosquitoes than usual to survive. The unusually high temperatures of the scorching summer that followed increased their numbers further by speeding up their life cycle. The economic crisis may also have played a role. Homeowners who could not pay their bank loans were forced to abandon their houses, sometimes leaving behind swimming pools that became excellent mosquito breeding grounds.

__34__ Dallas County was not doing some of the key things that help slow the spread of West Nile, such as testing dead birds for the virus and setting out enough mosquito traps. Diseases like West Nile thus have as much to do with what officials fail to do as with climate.
zhTranslation: 西尼羅熱是一種病毒引起的疾病。病毒最先出現在鳥類身上，鳥把病毒傳給蚊子，蚊子再藉由叮咬把病毒傳染給人。大多數感染西尼羅病毒的人從頭到尾都不會出現症狀；至於有症狀的人，會在被叮咬後 2 到 14 天之間發病。感染的人當中，大約每 5 人就有 1 人會發燒、頭痛、全身痠痛，通常持續一個星期左右。每 150 人當中的 1 人就不幸得多，會高燒、顫抖、癱瘓，甚至昏迷。__31__
正因為這樣，2012 年夏天西尼羅病毒在美國大規模爆發，才會那麼令人害怕。德州達拉斯一帶的情況特別嚴重，那一年病毒在當地讓將近 400 人染病、19 人死亡。__32__ 有些居民表示反對，擔心這個對策的害處比疾病本身還大。
為什麼 2012 年夏天特別適合西尼羅病毒和傳播病毒的蚊子？__33__ 那年冬天極為溫和，讓比平常更多的蚊子活了下來。接下來的夏天又異常炎熱，高溫加快了蚊子的生命週期，蚊子的數量因此更多。經濟危機可能也有影響。繳不出銀行貸款的屋主只好棄屋離開，有時留下的游泳池就成了蚊子絕佳的繁殖場所。
__34__ 達拉斯郡就沒有做到幾項減緩西尼羅病毒擴散的關鍵措施，像是檢驗死鳥身上有沒有病毒、設置足夠的捕蚊器。因此，西尼羅熱這類疾病和官員該做卻沒做的事情關係密切，就跟它和氣候的關係一樣。

marks: Tea is now the most typical English drink, but it took about two hundred years to reach every home in Britain.
The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes.
As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, it finally spread to every corner of British society.
paras: Tea is now the most typical English drink, but it took about two hundred years to reach every home in Britain. Much of its early popularity came from a foreign princess, Catherine of Braganza, who married King Charles II in 1662. __31__

The fashion soon spread beyond the circle of the nobility to the middle classes. In London, tea became a popular drink at the coffeehouses, where people met to do business and discuss the news. __32__ It came with a high price tag, and the government taxed it heavily as well. Many workers drank it only at work, where employers served them a cup in midmorning, creating a lasting British custom, the “tea break.”

__33__ At the time, the rich usually ate nothing between lunch and dinner, which might not be served until eight o’clock. The Duchess of Bedford is often said to have started the custom by having tea with bread, butter, and cake at about four o’clock. Thin sandwiches, named after the eighteenth-century Earl of Sandwich, were soon added to the menu.

As tea became much cheaper during the nineteenth century, it finally spread to every corner of British society. __34__ Unlike the light afternoon tea of the rich, this filling evening meal came to be called “high tea.” Today, people in Britain drink tea at any time of the day, whether they are rich or poor.
zhTranslation: 茶是現在最典型的英國飲料，但它花了大約兩百年，才普及到英國的每一個家庭。茶在英國早期能流行起來，很大一部分要歸功於一位外國公主，也就是在 1662 年嫁給英王 Charles II 的 Catherine of Braganza。__31__
這股風氣很快就從貴族圈傳到了中產階級。在倫敦，茶成了咖啡館裡受歡迎的飲料，人們在那裡碰面談生意、討論時事。__32__ 茶的價格很高，政府還課以重稅。許多工人只有在工作時才喝得到茶，因為雇主會在上午工作到一半時請他們喝一杯，這也成了一項延續至今的英國習俗，也就是「喝茶休息時間」（tea break）。
__33__ 在那個時候，有錢人在午餐和晚餐之間通常什麼都不吃，而晚餐可能要到八點才開始。據說這個習慣是貝德福公爵夫人開始的：她在下午四點左右喝茶，配上麵包、奶油和蛋糕。不久之後，以十八世紀的三明治伯爵命名的薄片三明治，也加進了下午茶的菜單。
十九世紀茶變得便宜許多，終於傳遍了英國社會的每一個角落。__34__ 和有錢人簡單的下午茶不同，這一頓晚餐吃得很飽，後來就叫做「high tea」。現在，英國人不論貧富，一天裡任何時候都會喝茶。

title: 引水人的專業（The Expertise of Marine Pilots）

options.A: Marine pilotage is a job that demands a high level of skill as well as quick and independent thinking.
options.B: As the sea level rises and falls, the water in harbor channels may reverse direction.
options.C: A large ship that strays even slightly out of the channel can easily run aground.
options.D: A local professional called a marine pilot then guides the ship safely into the harbor.
options.E: Getting on board can be risky in itself, as pilots often climb a rope ladder from a small boat.

optionsZh.A: 引水這份工作需要高度的技術，也需要能迅速、獨立地思考。
optionsZh.B: 隨著海面升高、降低，港內航道的海水可能會倒轉方向流動。
optionsZh.C: 大型船隻只要稍微偏離航道，就很容易擱淺。
optionsZh.D: 接著由一位叫做引水人的在地專業人士，引導船隻安全進港。
optionsZh.E: 光是登船本身就有風險，因為引水人常常得從小船攀著繩梯爬上大船。

unusedExplanation.lead: E 談的也是引水人，`risky`（有風險的）看起來和第二段的擱淺、第四段的 `risk management`（風險管理）都接得上，文法和語氣也沒有問題。可是**全篇談的是「船隻進港為什麼需要引水人、這份工作要求什麼」，E 談的卻是「引水人自己登船時有什麼危險」。**所以四個空格都放不下它：

rows.want: 一句交代船長把船開到港外以後，進港這一段由誰負責
rows.why: E 沒有說誰負責引導船隻進港，引水人也還沒有出現，就先講他們怎麼爬上船

rows.want: 一句說明船偏離深水航道會出什麼事，後一句的船身、貨物受損才有原因
rows.why: E 的危險落在爬繩梯的引水人身上，不會讓船身和貨物受損

rows.want: 一句說明潮汐怎麼影響海流，後一句「漲潮的方法退潮不一定行得通」才有道理
rows.why: E 和潮汐、海流都沒有關係

rows.want: 一句說出這份工作需要哪些能力，後一句才能用 `Above all`（最重要的是）說出比這些都重要的一點
rows.why: E 講的是登船的危險，不是這份工作需要的能力；而且登船這件事要到第四段第三句才交代

unusedExplanation.summary: **這一篇多出來的 E 屬於「主題相同，切面不對」，和 115 學測多出來的 D 同一類。** 115 學測全篇問「什麼影響微笑」，D 答「微笑分幾種」；這一篇談的是船隻進港為什麼需要引水人、這份工作要求什麼，E 談的卻是引水人登船時自己的安危。至於 115 學測參考試卷多出來的 C，則屬於「切面對，卻沒有段落在等它」，和這一篇不同。
unusedExplanation.takeaway: 多出來的選項常常和某一格共用一個字（這一篇是 E 的 `risky` 和第四段的 `risk`）。遇到這種情況，要問兩句說的是不是同一件事：第四段的風險指的是船、港口和海洋環境的安全，E 的風險卻是引水人爬繩梯時自己的安全，意思對不上，就不是它。

paraLabels: 破題：船長只把船開到港外，進港改由引水人引導
引水人為什麼不可少：港口中間深、四周淺，船一偏離航道就會擱淺
更多難題：潮汐讓海流轉向，風也會改變船的方向
這份工作的要求：技術與獨立判斷，最重要的是風險管理
marks: A marine pilot, often a former ship captain, is an expert with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor.
In addition to shallow seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port.
paras: Ships are the lifeline of trade among countries. Almost everything, from food to machinery, comes by way of the sea in huge ships commanded by captains. But a ship’s captain usually guides the vessel only until it reaches the waters just outside a port, where it waits to enter the harbor. __31__

A marine pilot, often a former ship captain, is an expert with specialized knowledge of a particular port or harbor. The pilot is needed to direct large ships into a port, where deep channels are often surrounded by shallow seabeds. __32__ Both the ship and its cargo could then be badly damaged, and some kinds of cargo might be dangerous if released into the sea.

In addition to shallow seabeds, tide and wind pose further challenges for bringing ships into a port. __33__ The same strategy for docking a vessel during an incoming tide may not work during an outgoing tide. Also, the wind can significantly alter the direction of the ship and how it reacts, adding to the difficulty of docking it.

__34__ Above all, it is about risk management. A marine pilot goes on board at a crucial time and directs the vessel based on his or her knowledge of the port and the situation at hand. The pilot is responsible for not only the safety of the ship but also the protection of the port and the marine environment.
zhTranslation: 船舶是國際貿易的命脈。從糧食到機械，幾乎所有東西都是由船長指揮的巨型船隻經海路運來。不過，船長通常只把船開到港口外的水域，船就在那裡等候進港。__31__
引水人往往本身當過船長，是對某個港口有專門了解的專家。大型船隻進港需要引水人引導，因為港口常有深水航道，四周卻是較淺的海床。__32__ 這麼一來，船身和貨物都可能嚴重受損，有些貨物一旦流進海裡，還可能造成危害。
除了海床較淺，潮汐和風也讓船隻進港更加困難。__33__ 漲潮時讓船靠岸的方法，到了退潮時不一定行得通。此外，風也會大幅改變船的方向和反應，讓靠岸更加困難。
__34__ 最重要的是，這份工作講究的是風險管理。引水人在關鍵時刻登船，根據自己對港口和當下狀況的了解來指揮船隻。引水人不但要負責船的安全，也要保護港口和海洋環境。

title: 大象怎麼分辨敵友（How Elephants Spot Their Enemies）

options.A: Elephants can, and they use both sight and smell to tell dangerous people from harmless ones.
options.B: Elephants can be a serious threat to local farmers, since they often raid crops at night.
options.C: What the elephants saw mattered as well, but it made them angry rather than afraid.
options.D: Smell alone was enough for the elephants to tell the two groups apart.
options.E: When a threat can be seen but not smelled, the risk is lower.

optionsZh.A: 大象做得到，而且牠們會同時靠視覺和嗅覺，分辨哪些人危險、哪些人無害。
optionsZh.B: 大象可能對當地農民構成嚴重威脅，因為牠們常在夜裡闖進田裡吃作物。
optionsZh.C: 大象看到的東西也有影響，不過這時牠們的反應是生氣，而不是害怕。
optionsZh.D: 大象光靠氣味，就分辨得出這兩個族群。
optionsZh.E: 如果威脅看得到卻聞不到，風險就比較低。

unusedExplanation.lead: B 讀起來很順，談的也是大象和人之間的威脅，還和第一段的問句一樣用了 `can`、`threat`。問題是，**全篇問的是「大象能不能分辨哪些人對牠有威脅、靠什麼分辨」，B 說的卻是「大象對農民有什麼威脅」，方向正好相反。**所以四個空格都放不下：

rows.want: 回答問句的兩件事「做不做得到、怎麼做到」，並預告後面嗅覺、視覺兩部分
rows.why: B 雖然也用 `Elephants can` 開頭，說的卻是大象威脅農民，沒有回答大象能不能分辨人，也沒有提到任何一種感官

rows.want: 替第三段的氣味實驗下結論：大象光靠氣味就分辨得出兩個族群
rows.why: B 的 `farmers` 和第二段最後一句共用同一個字，接起來看似很順，卻沒有氣味，也沒有說大象分辨得出哪一個族群

rows.want: 從氣味轉到視覺，並點出大象這一次是生氣、不是害怕
rows.why: B 沒有顏色，也沒有生氣和害怕的對比

rows.want: 和「聞到」相對的「只看到」，提供 `Therefore` 需要的理由「風險比較低」
rows.why: B 說的是大象會吃農民的作物，推不出大象為什麼不逃、反而生氣

paraLabels: 破題：問動物能不能分辨敵友、怎麼分辨，再以大象作答：靠視覺與嗅覺
背景：肯亞的兩個族群，一個有時會獵殺大象，一個大多務農
嗅覺：光靠氣味就分辨得出兩族，聞到馬賽族的衣服就逃開
視覺：看到沒人穿過的紅色衣服反而發怒，紅色是馬賽族年輕男性常穿的顏色
解釋：聞到表示危險就在附近，只看到表示風險低，所以反應不同
marks: In Kenya, researchers studied how elephants respond to men from two local ethnic groups, the Maasai and the Kamba.
The researchers believe that the elephants react differently because they interpret smells and sights in different ways.
paras: Most of us find it easy to tell our friends from our enemies. But can other animals tell which humans pose a threat to them, and if so, how? __31__

In Kenya, researchers studied how elephants respond to men from two local ethnic groups, the Maasai and the Kamba. The Maasai raise cattle, and their young men sometimes spear elephants to prove their manhood. The Kamba are mainly farmers and pose little danger to the animals.

__32__ The researchers placed clothing near groups of elephants; some pieces were clean, while others had been worn for five days by a Maasai or a Kamba man. When the elephants smelled clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away faster and farther than they did from the other pieces. They also took longer to relax afterward and headed for tall grass. Because they never came close enough to see the clothing, its scent was the only clue they had.

__33__ In the same study, the elephants were shown clean red and white clothing. They behaved far more aggressively toward the red pieces than toward the white ones. Red is the color young Maasai men typically wear.

The researchers believe that the elephants react differently because they interpret smells and sights in different ways. Smelling a potential danger means that a threat is nearby, so the best thing to do is run away and hide. __34__ Therefore, instead of showing fear and running away, the elephants express their anger and become aggressive.
zhTranslation: 我們大多數人都能輕易分辨誰是朋友、誰是敵人。但其他動物分辨得出哪些人對牠們有威脅嗎？如果分辨得出，又是怎麼做到的？__31__
研究人員在肯亞觀察大象面對當地兩個族群的男性時有什麼反應，這兩個族群是馬賽族和坎巴族。馬賽族以養牛為生，族裡的年輕男性有時會用長矛獵殺大象，證明自己是男子漢。坎巴族則大多務農，對大象沒什麼危險。
__32__ 研究人員把衣服放在象群附近，有的是乾淨的衣服，有的是馬賽族或坎巴族男性穿了五天的衣服。大象聞到馬賽族男性穿過的衣服時，離開的速度比聞到其他衣服時更快，走得也更遠。牠們事後也要花更久的時間才放鬆下來，而且會往高高的草叢走。由於大象始終沒有靠近到看得見衣服，氣味是牠們唯一的線索。
__33__ 在同一項研究中，研究人員讓大象看乾淨的紅色衣服和白色衣服。大象對紅色衣服表現出的攻擊性，遠比對白色衣服強。紅色正是馬賽族年輕男性常穿的顏色。
研究人員認為，大象會有不同的反應，是因為牠們對氣味和視覺的解讀不同。聞到潛在的危險，表示威脅就在附近，所以最好的辦法就是逃跑、躲起來。__34__ 因此，大象不是表現出害怕、逃開，而是表現出憤怒，變得具有攻擊性。

title: 動物發光的用途（What Living Lights Are For）

options.A: On land, the best-known glowing animals are fireflies, small beetles that flash to attract a mate.
options.B: Some deep-sea squid even release a cloud of glowing liquid to confuse an approaching predator.
options.C: On land as in the sea, living lights can be used to deceive other animals.
options.D: The flashes can help them communicate with their own kind, lure prey, or escape from predators.
options.E: To turn its lights off, a fish slides two black lids up to cover them.

optionsZh.A: 在陸地上，最為人熟知的發光動物是螢火蟲；牠們是一種小甲蟲，靠閃光吸引配偶。
optionsZh.B: 有些深海烏賊甚至會噴出一團會發光的液體，迷惑逼近的捕食者。
optionsZh.C: 在陸地上和在海裡一樣，生物發出的光也可以用來欺騙其他動物。
optionsZh.D: 這些閃光可以幫助牠們和同類溝通、引誘獵物，或逃離捕食者。
optionsZh.E: 燈眼魚要關燈的時候，會把兩片黑色的蓋子往上拉，蓋住頭燈。

rows.want: 把前一句說的「好幾個原因」一一列出來，也就是動物閃光的用途

rows.why: 第三段後面四句講的是陸地上的螢火蟲怎麼配對，B 講的卻是海裡的烏賊怎麼脫身，沒有從海裡轉到陸地

marks: Some fish produce light in the blackness of the sea.
paras: Some animals have organs in their bodies that produce light. Most of them live in the sea, but some live on land. When it is dark, they flash their lights on and off for a number of reasons. __31__

Some fish produce light in the blackness of the sea. When night falls over the Red Sea, tiny flashlight fish swim up from deep water to feed, each with a pair of “headlamps,” one beneath each eye. The light comes from bacteria that live inside the headlamps and glow all the time. __32__ By blinking their lights, the fish communicate with one another, and a fish guarding its home area blinks faster when an intruder comes near. When a predator approaches, a flashlight fish swims slowly in one direction with its lights on, then blinks them off and darts away in another direction.

__33__ After darkness falls in some parts of North America, female fireflies wait in the grass. The males fly overhead, flashing light from the undersides of their bodies. As there are many species of firefly, the males of each kind flash their own particular signal. Recognizing the flashing code of her own species, a female flashes back to one of the males, and he lands beside her.

__34__ When they are hungry, some female fireflies lure the males of other species to them. They flash a false reply when these males signal overhead, but eat the males as soon as they land. Eating the males also gives the females chemicals that protect them from spiders.

在漆黑的海裡，有些魚會發光。夜幕籠罩紅海時，小小的燈眼魚從深水處游上來覓食，每一條都有一對「頭燈」，兩隻眼睛下方各一個。頭燈的光來自住在裡面的細菌，這些細菌一直在發光。__32__ 燈眼魚靠著讓光一明一滅彼此溝通；守著自己地盤的燈眼魚，有外來者靠近時，閃光就會變快。捕食者逼近的時候，燈眼魚會先亮著燈朝一個方向慢慢游，接著突然關燈，再往另一個方向迅速游走。
__33__ 在北美洲的一些地方，天黑以後，雌螢火蟲在草叢裡等待，雄螢火蟲則在上空飛，從身體下方發出閃光。因為螢火蟲有許多種，每一種的雄蟲都發出自己特有的訊號。雌蟲認出自己這一種的閃光密碼，就閃光回應其中一隻雄蟲，那隻雄蟲就降落在牠身旁。
__34__ 有些雌螢火蟲餓了，會把其他種類的雄螢火蟲引誘過來。這些雄蟲在上空發出訊號時，雌蟲就送出假的回應，等雄蟲一降落，就把雄蟲吃掉。吃下這些雄蟲，雌蟲還能得到一些化學物質，保護自己不被蜘蛛吃掉。

options.A: Despite being close relatives, the okapi and the giraffe are not hard to tell apart.
options.B: The okapi first appeared in Western writing in 1890, when explorer Henry Morton Stanley mentioned a strange “African donkey.”
options.C: Okapis are shy animals that live alone deep in Congo’s rainforests and are rarely seen.
options.D: It was only later, when okapi skulls were examined, that naturalists realized the animal was related to the giraffe.
options.E: Yet its image is everywhere in the Democratic Republic of Congo, its only home in the wild.

optionsZh.B: 霍加狓第一次出現在西方人的著作裡，是在 1890 年：探險家 Henry Morton Stanley 提到了一種奇怪的「非洲驢」。

marks: Although the okapi has striped markings like those of a zebra, it is most closely related to the giraffe.
But decades of political turbulence have let many of Congo’s natural resources slip out of the government’s control, and okapi numbers have fallen by more than half since 1995.
paras: The okapi is a mammal living in one of the most biodiverse areas of central Africa. The animal was little known to the Western world until the early 20th century, and it is often described as half-zebra, half-giraffe, as if it were a mixed-breed creature from a Greek legend. __31__ The okapi is to the country what the giant panda is to China or the kangaroo to Australia.

Although the okapi has striped markings like those of a zebra, it is most closely related to the giraffe. It has a long neck and large, flexible ears. Its face and throat are grayish white. Its coat ranges from chocolate to reddish brown, in sharp contrast with the white horizontal stripes and rings on its legs and its white ankles. __32__ The okapi is much smaller, about the size of a horse, and looks more like a deer than a giraffe. While both male and female giraffes have horns, only male okapis do.

__33__ In the years that followed, Europeans in Africa heard more stories of an animal that they came to call the “African unicorn.” Explorers may have caught only a fleeting glimpse of its striped backside as it fled into the bushes, leading to speculation that it was some sort of rainforest zebra. Some even believed that the okapi was a new species of zebra. __34__

In 1992, the Okapi Wildlife Reserve was established in northeastern Congo to protect this rare mammal. But decades of political turbulence have let many of Congo’s natural resources slip out of the government’s control, and okapi numbers have fallen by more than half since 1995. Today, perhaps only 10,000 to 15,000 remain.
zhTranslation: 霍加狓是一種哺乳動物，生活在中非生物多樣性最豐富的地區之一。一直到 20 世紀初，西方世界對這種動物都所知不多；人們常形容牠半斑馬、半長頸鹿，好像牠是希臘神話裡由不同動物混合而成的生物。__31__ 霍加狓對這個國家的意義，就像大貓熊之於中國、袋鼠之於澳洲。
雖然霍加狓身上的條紋和斑馬很像，牠的親緣關係卻和長頸鹿最近。霍加狓的脖子很長，耳朵又大又靈活，臉和喉嚨是灰白色。身上的毛從巧克力色到紅棕色都有，和腿上白色的橫紋、環紋以及白色的腳踝，形成強烈的對比。__32__ 霍加狓的體型小得多，大約和馬一樣大，看起來也比較像鹿，不像長頸鹿。長頸鹿公的母的都有角，霍加狓卻只有公的才有。
__33__ 之後幾年，在非洲的歐洲人又聽到更多傳聞，說有一種動物，他們後來把牠叫做「非洲獨角獸」。探險家看到的，可能只是這種動物逃進樹叢時一閃而過的條紋臀部，於是有人猜測牠是某種雨林斑馬，有些人甚至相信霍加狓是新品種的斑馬。__34__
1992 年，剛果東北部設立了霍加狓野生動物保護區，保護這種稀有的哺乳動物。但是數十年的政治動盪，讓剛果許多天然資源脫離了政府的掌控，霍加狓的數量從 1995 年以來減少了一半以上。如今大概只剩下一萬到一萬五千隻。

title: 社會連結與心臟健康（The Power of Social Connection）

options.B: Staying close to family and friends may protect anyone’s heart, not just the hearts of Japanese men.
options.C: What did seem to matter was how closely the men held on to Japanese ways of life.
options.D: Doctors have long advised that a diet low in fatty meat can help protect the heart.
options.E: The farther from Japan the men lived, the more likely they were to have heart disease.

optionsZh.A: 他們的心臟病發生率，遠低於美國和歐洲的男性。
optionsZh.B: 和家人朋友保持親近，可能對每個人的心臟都有保護作用，不只是日本男性。
optionsZh.C: 看起來真正有關的，是這些男性保留日本生活方式的程度。
optionsZh.D: 醫生長久以來一直建議，少吃油脂多的肉，有助於保護心臟。
optionsZh.E: 這些男性住的地方離日本越遠，得心臟病的可能就越大。

paraLabels: 破題：日本男性多半抽菸，心臟病卻很少
研究：比較住在日本、夏威夷、加州的日裔男性
排除：常見的危險因子和飲食都解釋不完差距
轉折：真正有關的是傳統生活與緊密的團體
結論：每個人都需要真實世界裡的歸屬感
marks: In the 1960s and 1970s, Japanese men posed a puzzle for public health researchers.
Researchers in the United States and Japan set out to find the answer.
The usual risk factors, such as high blood pressure and cholesterol, explained some of the gap between the groups, but not all of it.
paras: In the 1960s and 1970s, Japanese men posed a puzzle for public health researchers. Most of them smoked, and smoking is one of the strongest risk factors for heart disease. __31__ What, then, was protecting their hearts?

Researchers in the United States and Japan set out to find the answer. They studied nearly 12,000 men of Japanese descent between the ages of 45 and 69. The men lived in Japan, Hawaii, or California, so the researchers could compare people with the same roots in three very different places. __32__

The usual risk factors, such as high blood pressure and cholesterol, explained some of the gap between the groups, but not all of it. Diet was another obvious suspect, since many of the men in America had switched from rice and fish to hamburgers and fries. Yet even the change in diet left part of the gap unexplained.

__33__ A second study of about 3,800 Japanese Americans in California found that the most traditional men had as little heart disease as men in Japan. They had been raised in Japanese culture and belonged to close-knit groups whose members supported one another. Among men who had adopted a Western way of life with looser social ties, the rate was three to five times higher.

The researchers suggested that close-knit groups may have protected the men from stress, which can harm the heart. __34__ We need to feel part of something bigger in order to thrive. And we need that sense of belonging not only online but in the real world of hugs, handshakes, and pats on the back.
zhTranslation: 在 1960 和 1970 年代，日本男性讓公共衛生研究人員想不通。他們大多抽菸，而抽菸是心臟病最主要的危險因子之一。__31__ 那麼，保護他們心臟的究竟是什麼？
美國和日本的研究人員著手尋找答案。他們研究了將近 12,000 名日裔男性，年齡在 45 到 69 歲之間。這些男性分別住在日本、夏威夷和加州，所以研究人員可以比較同樣出身、卻住在三個截然不同地方的人。__32__
高血壓、膽固醇這些常見的危險因子，可以解釋各組之間一部分的差距，卻不是全部。飲食是另一個明顯的可能原因，因為住在美國的男性，很多人已經從吃米飯和魚，改吃漢堡和薯條。可是，就連飲食的改變，也還有一部分差距解釋不了。
__33__ 另一項研究調查了加州大約 3,800 名日裔美國人，發現最傳統的那一群人，心臟病和日本本地的男性一樣少。他們從小在日本文化中長大，也屬於關係緊密、成員彼此扶持的團體。至於改採西方生活方式、社會關係比較鬆散的人，心臟病的比率則高出三到五倍。
研究人員認為，關係緊密的團體可能保護了這些男性，讓他們少受壓力的影響，而壓力會傷害心臟。__34__ 我們需要覺得自己屬於某個更大的群體，才能過得好。而且我們需要的歸屬感，不只在網路上，也要在真實的世界裡，在擁抱、握手和拍拍肩膀之中。

1940、50 年代：節目搬上電視，替忙碌的家庭示範方便快速的做法

marks: American cooking programs have taught audiences, changed audiences, and changed with audiences from generation to generation.
Cooking shows moved to television in the 1940s.
By the 1990s, cooking shows covered everything from elegant restaurant dishes to healthy home meals.
In the early 21st century, new shows were created to please audiences who loved celebrities and reality TV.
paras: American cooking programs have taught audiences, changed audiences, and changed with audiences from generation to generation. In October 1926, the United States Department of Agriculture created a fictional radio host named Aunt Sammy. Over the radio, she gave homemakers advice on all kinds of household matters, but it was mostly her recipes that caught listeners’ attention. The show helped spread cooking tips and led to a nationwide exchange of recipes.

Cooking shows moved to television in the 1940s. By the 1950s, they were often hosted by a cook who explained step by step how to prepare a dish. __31__ Poppy Cannon, for example, was the popular author of “The Can-Opener Cookbook.” She appeared on television, using canned foods to show how to cook quickly and easily.

__32__ Over time, cooking shows grew less fancy and began to feature dishes from all over the world. One well-known example is Martin Yan’s “Yan Can Cook,” which began airing on American public television in 1982. On the show, Yan taught Chinese cooking and signed off with the catchphrase “If Yan can cook, so can you!”
By the 1990s, cooking shows covered everything from elegant restaurant dishes to healthy home meals. Good food alone, however, was not enough to make a show a hit. __33__

In the early 21st century, new shows were created to please audiences who loved celebrities and reality TV. Some were filmed outside the studio, and many turned cooking into a contest between chefs. Top chefs have become as famous as rock stars. __34__ Cooking from a show’s recipes, as Aunt Sammy’s listeners once did, has gone out of style.
zhTranslation: 美國的烹飪節目一代又一代地教導觀眾、改變觀眾，也隨著觀眾而改變。1926 年 10 月，美國農業部創造了一位虛構的廣播主持人，名叫 Aunt Sammy（山姆阿姨）。她透過廣播，針對各種家務事給家庭主婦建議，不過最吸引聽眾注意的，主要還是她的食譜。這個節目幫忙傳播烹飪的訣竅，也促成了全國性的食譜交流。
烹飪節目在 1940 年代搬上了電視。到了 1950 年代，節目通常由一位廚師主持，一步一步說明一道菜怎麼做。__31__ 例如 Poppy Cannon 是《開罐器食譜》（The Can-Opener Cookbook）的作者，很受歡迎。她上電視時用罐頭食品示範怎麼快速、輕鬆地做菜。
__32__ 後來，烹飪節目沒那麼高檔了，開始介紹世界各地的菜色。一個有名的例子是甄文達（Martin Yan）的《甄能煮》（Yan Can Cook），這個節目 1982 年開始在美國的公共電視播出。他在節目裡教中國菜，每一集結尾都會說一句經典台詞：「甄能煮，你也能！」（If Yan can cook, so can you!）
到了 1990 年代，烹飪節目從餐廳的精緻料理到家裡的健康餐點都有。不過，光有好菜並不足以讓節目走紅。__33__
21 世紀初，業者推出新的節目，迎合喜歡名人、熱愛實境秀的觀眾。有些節目走出攝影棚拍攝，也有不少節目把做菜變成廚師之間的比賽。頂尖的廚師如今已經和搖滾巨星一樣有名。__34__ 像當年 Aunt Sammy 的聽眾那樣照著節目的食譜做菜，已經不流行了。

marks: One of the best-known technological aids in language teaching is the language laboratory.
When language labs first appeared, they were praised as a way to make language learning faster and more effective.
There were several reasons for the language lab’s failure to live up to expectations.
paras: One of the best-known technological aids in language teaching is the language laboratory. __31__ Students can record their own responses and play them back, while a teacher listens in and checks their progress.

When language labs first appeared, they were praised as a way to make language learning faster and more effective. They would take the burden of repetitive drills away from teachers, give learners more chances to practice listening and speaking, and let learners work at their own pace and keep track of their own progress. Many schools were quick to install the expensive equipment. __32__

There were several reasons for the language lab’s failure to live up to expectations. The recorded materials were often poorly designed, leaving students frustrated and bored. The published programs had little to do with the work students were doing in class. Few language teachers had received any training in designing materials or in running a lab. And once installed, the equipment proved difficult to maintain.
__33__ The newer labs contained much more than the traditional tape-based systems. Computer programs and video materials, in particular, proved extremely popular with learners.

__34__ For example, recordings can give learners a wide variety of natural, clearly recorded speech to help them sharpen their listening skills. Labs can also serve as resource centers, much like libraries, where learners get extra practice at a level they choose.
zhTranslation: 語言教學用到的科技輔助工具當中，最有名的之一就是語言教室。__31__ 學生可以錄下自己的回答再播放出來，老師則在一旁監聽，掌握他們的學習情形。
語言教室剛出現的時候，大家稱讚它能讓語言學習更快、更有效。語言教室可以替老師分擔反覆練習的工作，讓學習者有更多機會練習聽和說，也讓他們按照自己的步調學習，自己掌握學習進度。許多學校很快就裝設了昂貴的設備。__32__
語言教室沒有達到預期，原因有好幾個。錄音教材往往設計不良，讓學生覺得挫折又無聊。市面上出版的教材，和學生在課堂上學的內容沒什麼關係。很少語言老師受過設計教材或操作語言教室的訓練。而且設備一裝好，維護起來就很困難。
__33__ 新一代的語言教室，設備比過去以錄音帶為主的傳統系統豐富得多。其中電腦程式和影音教材，特別受到學習者歡迎。
__34__ 例如，錄音教材可以提供各式各樣自然、錄音清楚的語音，幫助學習者加強聽力。語言教室也可以像圖書館一樣當作資源中心，讓學習者按照自己選擇的程度多加練習。

paras: In 2020, Petur Oddsson, a power station worker in Iceland, was struck by a 60,000-volt current. The electric shock burned almost half of his body and melted away several layers of his skin. Burns this deep and extensive can be fatal. __31__

That treatment was one result of a larger effort in Iceland called “100% Fish.” As its name suggests, the project aims to put every part of each fish caught to use. It also hopes to change the fishing industry by encouraging new uses for fish.

__32__ In Iceland, as recently as 2003, people knew how to use only about 40% of each cod they caught. The rest, about 60% of the fish, went to waste. With the help of 100% Fish, Icelanders have now found uses for almost 95% of each cod.

Nearly every part of the fish now ends up in some kind of product. __33__ Dried fish heads and spines are shipped to West Africa, where they form the base of a protein-rich soup. Omega-3 capsules, sprays that help protect against colds, and dog snacks are made from parts that were once thrown away.

Iceland’s success depends largely on people from different fields working together. The project brings fishing companies together with universities, startups, and research teams. __34__ Each cod caught in Iceland is now worth far more than it used to be. The project also offers the world a useful model for making better use of natural resources.

這種療法，是冰島一項名為「100% Fish」的大型計畫的成果之一。正如名稱所示，這項計畫的目標是把捕到的每一條魚的每個部位都用上。計畫也希望鼓勵大家替魚找出新用途，藉此改變漁業。
__32__ 直到 2003 年，冰島人還只知道怎麼利用每條鱈魚的四成左右，其餘大約六成都浪費掉了。在 100% Fish 的帶動下，冰島人現在已經替一條鱈魚將近 95% 的部分找到了用途。
現在魚身上幾乎每個部位都會做成某種產品。__33__ 曬乾的魚頭和魚骨運到西非，在當地用來熬煮富含蛋白質的湯。至於 Omega-3 膠囊、預防感冒的噴劑和狗零食，原料也都是過去丟掉的部分。
冰島的成功，主要靠不同領域的人通力合作。這項計畫讓漁業公司和大學、新創公司以及研究團隊攜手合作。__34__ 如今冰島捕到的每一條鱈魚，價值都比過去高出許多。這項計畫也為全世界提供了一個實用的模式，讓各國更妥善地利用自然資源。

marks: Monopoly is a very popular board game around the world today, but little is known about its American inventor, Elizabeth Magie, and the philosophy behind her invention.
Born in 1866, Magie was a rebel against the norms and politics of her times.
The game soon became a hit on college campuses and among Quaker communities, and some people modified the game board.

paras: Monopoly is a very popular board game around the world today, but little is known about its American inventor, Elizabeth Magie, and the philosophy behind her invention.

Born in 1866, Magie was a rebel against the norms and politics of her times. Her thinking was shaped by the economist Henry George, who believed that all people should have an equal right to use the land, just as they have an equal right to breathe the air. __31__ In 1904, she patented her Landlord’s Game. The game board consisted of a circuit of streets and landmarks for sale.

__32__ Under the Prosperity rules, every player gained each time someone acquired a new property. The game was won (by all!) when the player starting with the least money doubled his or her fortune. Under the Monopolist rules, on the other hand, each player advanced by acquiring properties and collecting rent from all who landed there later. Whoever managed to bankrupt the other players won the game. The purpose of the dual sets of rules, said Magie, was for players to understand how these different approaches to property can lead to different social outcomes: “all win” or “win all.”
The game soon became a hit on college campuses and among Quaker communities, and some people modified the game board. __33__

However, when Parker Brothers learned of the game’s true origin, it bought Magie’s patent for only $500. The game was sold under the name Monopoly, with only the rules that let one player triumph over all the others, and it soon became a best seller. __34__ Thus a rags-to-riches myth was created, ironically exemplifying Monopoly’s implicit values: Chase wealth and crush your opponents if you want to come out on top.
zhTranslation: 大富翁是今天風行全世界的桌遊，但很少人知道它的美國發明人 Elizabeth Magie，也很少人知道她發明這款遊戲背後的理念。
Magie 生於 1866 年，是個反抗當時社會規範和政治的人。她的想法深受經濟學家 Henry George 影響；George 認為，人人都應該有平等使用土地的權利，就像人人都有呼吸空氣的權利一樣。__31__ 1904 年，她為自己的「地主遊戲」取得專利。遊戲的版面是一圈可以買賣的街道和地標。
__32__ 照繁榮規則玩，每當有人取得新的地產，每一位玩家都能獲益。等到起始資金最少的那位玩家財富翻倍，遊戲就算贏了（而且是大家一起贏！）。壟斷規則就不一樣了，玩家靠取得地產、向之後停在那裡的人收租來前進，能讓其他玩家全部破產的人就是贏家。Magie 說，設計兩套規則的用意，是讓玩家了解對待財產的方式不同，社會的結果也會不同：「大家都贏」或「贏家通吃」。
這款遊戲很快在大學校園和貴格會社群流行起來，有些人還修改了遊戲版面。__33__
不過，Parker Brothers 得知遊戲真正的起源以後，只花 500 美元就買下 Magie 的專利。這款遊戲改用大富翁（Monopoly）這個名字販售，只保留讓一個玩家打敗其他所有人的規則，很快就成了暢銷商品。__34__ 一段白手起家的神話就這樣誕生了；諷刺的是，這段神話正好體現了大富翁隱含的價值觀：想要出人頭地，就要追求財富、擊垮對手。

marks: Now the bright green plant is being put to a new use: producing renewable energy.
For years, only its soft, edible flesh was used.
paras: The prickly pear cactus is such a powerful symbol in Mexico that it occupies a prime spot on the country’s national flag. The plant was considered sacred by the ancient Aztecs, and modern-day Mexicans eat it, drink it, and even use it in medicines and shampoos. Now the bright green plant is being put to a new use: producing renewable energy.
Known locally as nopal, the prickly pear is farmed on a massive scale in Mexico. For years, only its soft, edible flesh was used. __31__

Milpa Alta, a farming district in the south of Mexico City, grows about 200,000 tons of prickly pear a year. Up to 10 tons of it ends up as waste on the floor of the local cactus market every day. __32__ Its biogas generator, set up at the market as a pilot project, turns cactus skins into gas that can be used to make electricity. Vendors there welcome this new way to use skins that once went straight into the trash.

__33__ For one thing, only the skin of the cactus is used for fuel, while the inner flesh is still eaten. Using the plant as a fuel source will therefore not push up food prices. The cactus also needs very little water, so it can grow on dry land that is unsuited to most food crops. As a result, it does not take water or farmland away from food production.

__34__ City officials would like to set up similar generators at other produce markets in the capital. If the project can be expanded in this way, the prickly pear could be the key to Mexico’s energy future.
zhTranslation: 仙人掌在墨西哥是極具分量的象徵，甚至在墨西哥國旗上占了顯要的位置。古代阿茲特克人把這種植物視為神聖，現代的墨西哥人會吃仙人掌、喝仙人掌汁，甚至拿它來做藥品和洗髮精。如今，這種鮮綠色的植物又有了新用途：生產再生能源。
這種仙人掌在當地叫做 nopal，在墨西哥大量種植。多年來，人們只用它柔軟、可以吃的嫩肉。__31__

paras: Researchers in Japan have fitted a train with a speaker that barks like a dog and snorts like a deer. The unusual noises are meant to drive deer away from the tracks before the train can hit them.
On Japan’s railways, collisions with deer have become a common and serious problem. __31__ Each time, trains were stopped or delayed for at least 30 minutes.

Deer are drawn to railway lines because they need iron in their diets. They lick the rails to pick up iron filings produced as the wheels grind against the tracks. Over the years, several ways of scaring them off have been tried. __32__

The new device, developed by a team at Japan’s Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI), relies on sound rather than sight or smell. According to RTRI researchers, deer repeatedly give short, shrill snorts to warn one another of danger. __33__ The team added the barking of a dog, an animal that deer greatly fear. When deer hear a 3-second snort followed by about 20 seconds of barking, they panic and run away from the tracks.

__34__ Encouraged by the outcome, RTRI now plans to set up fixed barking devices where deer are often seen. Officials have promised, though, that the noises will not be played in areas where people live beside the tracks.
zhTranslation: 日本的研究人員在一列火車上裝了喇叭，可以發出狗吠聲，也可以發出鹿的鼻息聲。這些不尋常的聲音，是要在火車撞上鹿之前，先把鹿從鐵軌旁趕走。
在日本的鐵路上，火車撞到鹿已經成了常見又嚴重的問題。__31__ 每一次，列車都停駛或延誤了至少 30 分鐘。
鹿之所以靠近鐵路，是因為飲食中需要鐵質。車輪和鐵軌摩擦會產生鐵屑，鹿就舔鐵軌來攝取這些鐵屑。這些年來，人們試過好幾種把鹿嚇走的方法。__32__
這個新裝置是日本鐵道綜合技術研究所（RTRI）的團隊開發的，它靠的是聲音，而不是視覺或嗅覺。RTRI 的研究人員說，鹿會反覆發出短促尖銳的鼻息聲，警告同伴有危險。__33__ 研究團隊又加上了鹿非常害怕的狗吠聲。鹿聽到 3 秒的鼻息聲、接著大約 20 秒的狗吠聲，就會驚慌地逃離鐵軌。
__34__ 研究所受到這個結果鼓舞，現在打算在鹿常出現的地方設置固定的狗吠裝置。不過，相關人員保證，鐵軌旁有住家的地區不會播放這些聲音。

marks: This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink.
For the yellow-bellied sea snake, which usually spends all of its time far from land, rain is the only source of fresh water.
paras: Many marine animals, including penguins and marine iguanas, have evolved special glands to get rid of excess salt. In penguins these glands sit just above the eyes, and marine iguanas sneeze the salt out through their noses. Sea snakes have salt glands too, under their tongues, but these glands cannot handle the massive amounts of salt that would enter their bodies if they actually drank seawater. This poses a serious problem when it comes to getting enough water to drink. If seawater is not an option, how do these snakes survive in the ocean?

For the yellow-bellied sea snake, which usually spends all of its time far from land, rain is the only source of fresh water. When it rains, a thin layer of fresh water forms on top of the ocean. __31__

An international team of researchers focused on a population of yellow-bellied sea snakes in the Pacific waters off Costa Rica, where the dry season can last six or seven months. During those dry months, the snakes presumably have nothing to drink. __32__

The researchers collected more than 500 of the snakes and weighed them. During the dry season, nearly half of the snakes drank the fresh water the team offered them, while almost none did in the wet season. __33__ Thinner, more withered snakes were more likely to drink, and they drank more. Finally, as predicted, snakes captured in the dry season contained significantly less body water than those scooped up in the wet season.

__34__ The snakes may stay dehydrated for six or seven months at a time. Scientists believe that dehydration at sea, especially during long droughts, may explain why sea snake numbers are falling in some parts of the world.
zhTranslation: 許多海洋動物，例如企鵝和海鬣蜥，都演化出特殊的腺體來排除多餘的鹽分。企鵝的這種腺體長在眼睛上方，海鬣蜥則是靠打噴嚏，把鹽分從鼻孔噴出來。海蛇也有鹽腺，位置在舌頭下方，可是牠如果真的喝下海水，大量的鹽分進入體內，這些腺體就應付不了。這麼一來，要喝到足夠的水就成了一個嚴重的問題。既然不能喝海水，海蛇要怎麼在海洋裡活下去呢？
黃腹海蛇通常一直待在遠離陸地的海上，對牠來說，雨水是唯一的淡水來源。下雨時，海面上會形成一層薄薄的淡水。__31__
一個國際研究團隊鎖定哥斯大黎加外海（太平洋）的一群黃腹海蛇，當地的乾季可能長達六、七個月。在這幾個乾旱的月份裡，海蛇大概沒有東西可以喝。__32__
研究人員捕捉了 500 多條這種海蛇，並替牠們秤重。乾季時，將近一半的海蛇會喝研究團隊提供的淡水；到了雨季，幾乎沒有一條會喝。__33__ 越瘦、越乾癟的海蛇越可能喝水，喝的量也越多。最後，一如預期，乾季捕獲的海蛇體內水分明顯比雨季撈到的少。
__34__ 海蛇可能一次就脫水長達六、七個月。科學家認為，海上脫水（尤其是在長期乾旱的時候）或許可以解釋世界上某些地區的海蛇為什麼越來越少。

用意：prom 這個字的由來，以及大人為什麼重視舞會
演變：從體育館裡的簡樸聚會，變成大肆消費的場合

marks: In the United States, parents and educators have come to regard the prom as an important lesson in social skills.
paras: The high school prom is the first formal social event for most American teenagers. It has also been a rite of passage for young Americans for about a century.

The word “prom” was first used in the 1890s for formal dances at which guests would display their fashions and dancing skills during the evening’s grand march. In the United States, parents and educators have come to regard the prom as an important lesson in social skills. __31__

The first high school proms were held in the 1920s. By the 1930s, proms had become common across the country. __32__ Prom-goers were well dressed but not fancily dressed up for the occasion: boys wore jackets and ties, and girls their Sunday dresses. Couples danced to music provided by a local amateur band or a record player. After the 1960s, and especially since the 1980s, the prom in many areas has become a serious exercise in excessive consumption, with boys renting expensive tuxedos and girls wearing designer gowns. Stretch limousines are often hired to drive prom-goers to expensive restaurants or discos for an all-night extravaganza.
__33__ Many of them worry about their self-image and about fitting in with their peers. Prom night can be a dreadful experience for socially awkward teens or for those who fail to find a date.
__34__ There have been reports, for example, of proms organized by and for homeless youth. There have also been “couple-free” proms, to which all students are welcome.
zhTranslation: 對大多數美國青少年來說，高中畢業舞會是他們第一次參加的正式社交活動。大約一百年來，畢業舞會也一直是美國年輕人的成年禮。
prom 這個字最早在 1890 年代出現，指的是正式的舞會，賓客會在晚上開場的列隊進場（grand march）中展示自己的服裝和舞技。在美國，家長和教育工作者逐漸把畢業舞會看作學習社交技巧的重要一課。__31__

美國最早的高中畢業舞會在 1920 年代舉行。到了 1930 年代，畢業舞會已經遍及全國。__32__ 參加舞會的人穿著得體，但不會為了這個場合刻意盛裝打扮：男生穿外套、打領帶，女生穿上做禮拜時穿的洋裝。一對對舞伴隨著當地業餘樂團或唱機播放的音樂跳舞。1960 年代以後，尤其是 1980 年代以來，許多地區的畢業舞會變成了大肆消費的場合，男生租昂貴的晚禮服，女生穿名牌禮服。參加舞會的人還常常租加長型禮車，載他們到高價的餐廳或舞廳，狂歡一整夜。
__33__ 其中很多人擔心自己的形象，也擔心能不能融入同儕。對不擅社交的青少年，或是找不到舞伴的人來說，畢業舞會那一晚可能是很可怕的經驗。
__34__ 例如，有報導提到由無家可歸的青少年籌辦、也專為他們舉辦的舞會。另外也有「不需舞伴」的舞會，歡迎所有學生參加。

定義：先點出常見的誤解，再說明催眠是高度專注的狀態
差異：不是每個人都一樣容易被催眠
研究：大腦掃描看到的變化
應用：從研究結果到取代止痛藥的期望
marks: Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers.
paras: When Dr. David Spiegel emerged from a three-hour shoulder surgery in 1972, he did not use any pain medication to recover. __31__ It worked—to the surprise of everyone but Spiegel himself, who has studied hypnosis for 45 years.

Hypnosis is often misunderstood as a kind of sleep in which a person does whatever he or she is told to do. __32__ When hypnotized, you tune out most of the stimuli around you. You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought. This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.

__33__ In a recent study, Spiegel and his colleagues found that people who are easily hypnotized tend to be more trusting of others, more intuitive, and more likely to get caught up in a good movie. The research team compared people who were highly hypnotizable with those low in hypnotizability.

Both groups were given fMRI scans under several different conditions: at rest, while recalling a memory, and during two sessions of hypnosis. The researchers saw some interesting changes in the brain during hypnosis—but only in the highly hypnotizable group. __34__

This helps explain how hypnosis can have powerful effects, including reducing stress, anxiety, pain, and self-consciousness. Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers. His own earlier research has shown that when people in pain were taught self-hypnosis, they needed half as much pain medication and suffered half as much pain as those who were only given painkillers. However, more needs to be learned about hypnosis before its full potential can be harnessed.
zhTranslation: 1972 年，David Spiegel 醫師動完三個小時的肩部手術，復原期間沒有用任何止痛藥。__31__ 結果真的有效。除了研究催眠已經 45 年的 Spiegel 本人，大家都很驚訝。
很多人誤以為催眠是一種睡眠，人在這種狀態下，別人叫他做什麼，他就做什麼。__32__ 處在催眠狀態時，你會把周遭大部分的刺激都摒除在外。你會全神貫注在眼前的事情上，幾乎不去想任何別的事情。這種恍惚般的狀態，可以是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具。
__33__ Spiegel 和同事在最近一項研究中發現，容易被催眠的人往往比較信任別人，比較依賴直覺，看到一部好電影，也比較容易沉浸其中。研究團隊把很容易催眠的人和不容易催眠的人拿來做比較。
兩組人都在幾種不同的情況下接受功能性磁振造影（fMRI）掃描：休息時、回想一段記憶時，以及兩次催眠過程中。研究人員看到大腦在催眠時出現一些有趣的變化，但只出現在很容易催眠的那一組。__34__
這有助於解釋催眠為什麼能有強大的效果，包括減輕壓力、焦慮、疼痛，以及在意別人眼光的不自在。Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥。他自己先前的研究顯示，身體疼痛的人學了自我催眠以後，和只拿到止痛藥的人相比，需要的止痛藥只有一半，感受到的疼痛也只有一半。不過，我們對催眠還需要更多了解，才能充分發揮它的潛力。

marks: But it was the running machine, the ancestor of the modern bicycle, that made him famous.
The running machine, also known as the Draisine or the hobby horse, was a very primitive bicycle.
The success of the hobby horse was short-lived, though.
paras: Born in 1785 in southwestern Germany, Baron Karl Drais was one of the most creative German inventors of the 19th century. The baron’s numerous inventions include an early keyboard typewriter, the meat grinder, and a device to record piano music on paper. But it was the running machine, the ancestor of the modern bicycle, that made him famous.

The running machine, also known as the Draisine or the hobby horse, was a very primitive bicycle. With no chain or pedals, it moved only when riders pushed off the ground with their feet. The frame and wheels were made of wood. __31__ It was the first vehicle with two wheels placed one behind the other. Riders also steered it with a bar much like a modern handlebar.

__32__ Horses cost a lot to buy, and they had to be fed even when they were not being used. A muscle-powered two-wheeler, he believed, could replace them and let large numbers of people travel faster than on foot.

Drais made his first recorded ride on June 12, 1817, covering 13 kilometers in about an hour. The same trip usually took a horse-drawn mail coach four hours. The next year, Drais introduced the machine in Paris, where it quickly caught on. Riders in Britain were soon racing on their own copies of it. __33__

The success of the hobby horse was short-lived, though. The machines were heavy and difficult to ride. Safety was an issue, too, because riders often sped along the sidewalks. Collisions with unsuspecting pedestrians were frequent, and within a few years many European and American cities had banned the machine. __34__ Decades later, in the 1860s, French inventors added pedals to the front wheel and took a big step toward the modern bicycle.
zhTranslation: Karl Drais 男爵 1785 年生於德國西南部，是 19 世紀德國最有創意的發明家之一。這位男爵的發明很多，包括早期一種有鍵盤的打字機、絞肉機，還有一種能把鋼琴音樂記錄在紙上的裝置。不過，讓他成名的是現代自行車的始祖：滑行車（running machine）。
滑行車又叫 Draisine 或 hobby horse，是一種非常原始的自行車。它沒有鏈條，也沒有踏板，騎的人要用雙腳蹬地，車子才會前進。車架和輪子都是木頭做的。__31__ 它是第一輛把兩個輪子前後排成一直線的車。騎的人也用一根很像現代把手的橫桿來控制方向。
__32__ 馬買起來很貴，就算沒在用，也還是得餵。他相信，一輛靠人力推動的兩輪車可以取代馬，讓許多人移動得比走路還快。
1817 年 6 月 12 日，Drais 第一次有紀錄的試騎，大約一個小時就騎了 13 公里；同樣的路程，馬拉的郵務馬車通常要走四個小時。第二年，Drais 的滑行車在巴黎公開亮相，很快就在當地流行起來。不久，英國也有人騎著自己仿製的滑行車比賽。__33__
不過，滑行車的成功並不長久。這種車很重，也不好騎。安全也是問題，因為騎的人常在人行道上飛快騎過。滑行車常常撞上沒有防備的行人，幾年之內，歐洲和美國的許多城市都禁止使用這種車。__34__ 數十年後，到了 1860 年代，法國的發明家替滑行車的前輪裝上踏板，朝現代的自行車邁進了一大步。

marks: As a result, most anthems today are either hymns or marches played on European instruments.
In addition to hymns and marches, British composer Michael Bristow identifies two less common types.
Even an anthem that sounds traditional may owe a great deal to Europe, and Japan’s is a good example.
paras: Over the past three hundred years, a national anthem has been one of the first things a country establishes when it gains its freedom or independence. Anthems are generally performed at formal state occasions and at other events that celebrate the nation’s identity.

The Dutch song “Het Wilhelmus,” written in the 16th century, is often called the world’s oldest national anthem. Next came Britain’s “God Save the King,” a hymn that became popular in the 1740s. __31__ Many states, such as those that are now part of Germany, took the British hymn as their model. Others, notably Spain and France, chose marches, songs with a strong beat often played by military bands.
__32__ Even after former colonies gained independence, they often kept the traditions of their old rulers. As a result, most anthems today are either hymns or marches played on European instruments.

In addition to hymns and marches, British composer Michael Bristow identifies two less common types. National anthems in South and Central America are often operatic, with long, elaborate orchestral introductions. Italian opera of the 19th century shaped this style. __33__

Even an anthem that sounds traditional may owe a great deal to Europe, and Japan’s is a good example. In 1869, John William Fenton, a British bandmaster living in Japan, noticed that the country had no national anthem. A Japanese military officer, Ōyama Iwao, chose the words from a classic Japanese poem, and Fenton set them to music. __34__ Yet it was a German musician, Franz Eckert, who gave the new tune Western harmony. The anthem Japan sings today therefore combines a tune by Japanese composers with European harmony.
zhTranslation: 過去三百年來，一個國家取得自由或獨立的時候，最先確立的事情之一，往往就是國歌。國歌通常在國家的正式場合演奏，也會出現在其他慶祝國家認同的活動上。
荷蘭的〈威廉頌〉（Het Wilhelmus）寫於 16 世紀，常被稱為世界上最古老的國歌。接著是英國的〈天佑吾王〉（God Save the King），這是一首聖歌，在 1740 年代開始流行。__31__ 許多邦國，例如今天屬於德國的那些邦國，都以這首英國聖歌為範本。其他國家，特別是西班牙和法國，則選了進行曲，也就是節奏強烈、常由軍樂隊演奏的歌。
__32__ 前殖民地即使獨立了，也常常保留以前統治者的傳統。因此，今天大多數的國歌不是聖歌就是進行曲，而且用歐洲的樂器演奏。
除了聖歌和進行曲，英國作曲家 Michael Bristow 還歸納出兩種比較少見的類型。中南美洲的國歌常常帶有歌劇風格，前面有很長、很繁複的管弦樂前奏。這種風格受到 19 世紀義大利歌劇的影響。__33__

即使是聽起來很傳統的國歌，也可能深受歐洲影響，日本的國歌就是一個好例子。1869 年，住在日本的英國軍樂隊隊長 John William Fenton 注意到，這個國家沒有國歌。日本軍官大山巖（Ōyama Iwao）從一首日本古典詩歌選出歌詞，再由 Fenton 譜曲。__34__ 不過，替這首新曲子配上西式和聲的，卻是德國音樂家 Franz Eckert。因此，日本今天唱的國歌，是日本作曲家寫的旋律，配上歐洲的和聲。

paras: The Lego Group had a very humble beginning in the workshop of Ole Kirk Christiansen, a carpenter from Denmark. __31__ Local families liked them so much that he decided to make toys his main business. A few years later, he named the company Lego, from the Danish words leg godt, which mean “play well.”

In 1947, the company expanded into making plastic toys, and it soon began producing early versions of its building bricks. At first, retailers and customers did not think highly of them, since most people preferred toys made of wood or metal. Many of the company’s shipments were returned after poor sales. __32__

However, Christiansen’s son, Godtfred Kirk Christiansen, saw immense potential in the plastic bricks. He believed they could become a system for creative play. __33__ In 1958, the modern interlocking brick design was finally developed and patented. Small tubes underneath each brick now gripped the one below, so a model stayed in one piece until a child pulled it apart.

__34__ A castle could be taken apart and turned into a ship, and pieces from a new set fit the ones a child already had. By 2008, Lego was sold in more than 130 countries, and about seven Lego sets were sold every second.

Fans around the world celebrated the brick’s 50th anniversary that year. Over those fifty years, the brick itself had hardly changed. A brick made in 1958 still fits one made today, and that is probably why the toy has never fallen out of favor.

1947 年，公司擴大經營，開始做塑膠玩具，不久也開始生產早期的組合積木。起初，零售商和顧客都不太看好這些塑膠製品，因為大多數人比較喜歡木頭或金屬做的玩具。公司出的很多貨因為賣不好，都被退了回來。__32__
不過，Christiansen 的兒子 Godtfred Kirk Christiansen 看出這些塑膠積木有巨大的潛力。他相信這些積木可以變成一套激發創意的遊戲系統。__33__ 1958 年，現代的互扣式積木設計終於研發完成，也取得了專利。每塊積木底下的小管子會緊緊扣住下面那一塊，所以拼好的模型不會散開，要等孩子自己動手拆。

現象：島上哺乳類體型改變的模式，稱為福斯特法則
原因：大體型在大陸上有用，到了島上反而成為負擔
進一步：大型哺乳類縮小多少，要看是什麼樣的島
實例：澤西島的紅鹿縮小的幅度與速度
marks: The size and isolation of islands have a profound effect on island ecosystems and their inhabitants.
Scientists who study species evolution have found that mammals that settle on islands often end up a very different size from their relatives on the mainland.
A study of fossil elephants from islands around the world suggests that how much big mammals shrink depends on the kind of island they live on.
Red deer on Jersey, one of the Channel Islands about 14 miles off the coast of France, show how far and how fast big mammals can shrink.
paras: Islands are quite different from continents and other mainland areas. The size and isolation of islands have a profound effect on island ecosystems and their inhabitants.

Scientists who study species evolution have found that mammals that settle on islands often end up a very different size from their relatives on the mainland. __31__ This pattern, first described by J. Bristol Foster in 1964, is known as Foster’s rule, or the island effect. Although there are a number of exceptions, the trend generally holds true for both fossil species and mammals living on islands today.

__32__ In a mainland environment, being large is often a safer and more adaptive way for an animal to avoid predators. On an island, with few natural predators and less competition, being large is no longer an advantage. In fact, great size can become a burden, since a huge animal needs far more food to survive and reproduce.

A study of fossil elephants from islands around the world suggests that how much big mammals shrink depends on the kind of island they live on. On balanced islands with many kinds of animals, competition with other large plant-eaters often keeps big mammals from shrinking very much. __33__

Red deer on Jersey, one of the Channel Islands about 14 miles off the coast of France, show how far and how fast big mammals can shrink. When rising seas cut the island off from the mainland, a group of normal-sized red deer was trapped there. __34__ The whole process took less than 6,000 years.
zhTranslation: 島嶼和大陸，或其他大片陸地，有很大的不同。島嶼的面積和與世隔絕的環境，對島上的生態系和生物有深遠的影響。
研究物種演化的科學家發現，遷居到島上的哺乳類，最後體型往往和牠們在大陸上的親戚很不一樣。__31__ 這個模式在 1964 年由 J. Bristol Foster 首先提出，稱為福斯特法則，也叫島嶼效應。雖然有不少例外，但無論是化石物種，還是今天住在島上的哺乳類，大致上都符合這個趨勢。
__32__ 在大陸上，體型大往往是動物躲避掠食者比較安全、也比較能適應環境的方式。到了島上，天敵少、競爭也少，體型大就不再是優勢。事實上，體型大反而可能成為負擔，因為大型動物需要多得多的食物才能生存和繁衍。
一項研究分析了世界各地島嶼上的大象化石，結果顯示，大型哺乳類會縮小多少，要看牠們住在什麼樣的島上。在生態平衡、動物種類多的島上，和其他大型草食動物的競爭，往往讓大型哺乳類不至於縮小太多。__33__
海峽群島中的澤西島（Jersey）距離法國海岸約 14 英里，島上的紅鹿就說明了大型哺乳類能縮小到什麼程度、又能縮得多快。海平面上升，把這座島和大陸隔開的時候，有一群體型正常的紅鹿被困在島上。__34__ 整個過程花了不到 6,000 年。

發現：刺果的尖端是小鉤子，勾住布料的線圈，讓他想到可以做成扣件
開發：棉布不耐用，改用尼龍；取名、取得專利、開始量產
上市：起初賣得不好，1960 年代太空總署採用後人氣上升
今天：魔鬼氈隨處可見，連人工心臟都用得到
marks: Developing a real product took years of hard work.
paras: One fine morning in 1941, Swiss engineer George de Mestral went for a walk in the woods with his dog. When they got home, he found a lot of burrs from a wild plant stuck to the dog’s fur and to his pants. Curious about how they held on so tightly, he rushed to his microscope to take a closer look.

To the naked eye, the tips of the burrs looked straight. Under the microscope, though, he could see that each tip actually ended in a tiny hook. The hooks had caught on the small loops of thread in his pants and clung to them firmly. __31__

Developing a real product took years of hard work. De Mestral’s first challenge was finding a material strong enough for the job. __32__ Synthetic fibers turned out to be the answer, and he finally settled on nylon. The improved fastener had about 300 hooks in every square inch, so it stayed firmly closed yet could be pulled apart easily. He named it “Velcro,” from the French words velours (velvet) and crochet (hook). By 1955, he had patented his invention, and he soon began mass-producing it in factories in Europe and later in Canada and the United States.

__33__ Because most fashion critics found it ugly and cheap-looking, it was used mostly on sports equipment such as ski gear and diving suits. Its popularity grew quickly in the 1960s, when NASA began using it to keep objects from floating around in spacecraft.
__34__ It is used on clothing and shoes, children’s toys, airplane seat cushions, blood pressure cuffs, and surgical gowns. Most impressively, it even helped hold together the first artificial heart.
zhTranslation: 1941 年一個晴朗的早晨，瑞士工程師 George de Mestral 帶著狗到樹林裡散步。回到家後，他發現狗毛和自己的褲子上黏了許多野生植物的刺果。他很好奇這些刺果為什麼黏得這麼牢，於是立刻衝到顯微鏡前，想看個仔細。
用肉眼看，刺果的尖端是直的；可是在顯微鏡下，他看得出每個尖端其實都帶著一個小鉤子。這些鉤子勾住了褲子布料上的小線圈，緊緊附著不放。__31__

要開發出真正的產品，花了好幾年的心血。de Mestral 的第一個難題，是找到一種夠堅固、能勝任的材料。__32__ 結果發現合成纖維才是答案，他最後選定了尼龍。改良後的扣件每平方英寸大約有 300 個鉤子，所以能牢牢黏住，需要時又能輕鬆扯開。他把它取名為 Velcro，來自法文的 velours（天鵝絨）和 crochet（鉤子）。到了 1955 年，他已經為這項發明取得專利，不久就開始量產，先在歐洲設廠，後來又擴展到加拿大和美國。
__33__ 大多數時尚評論家覺得它很醜，看起來很廉價，所以它多半只用在滑雪裝備、潛水衣這類運動用品上。到了 1960 年代，美國太空總署開始用它來固定太空船裡的物品，免得東西到處飄，它的人氣也跟著快速上升。
__34__ 衣服和鞋子、兒童玩具、飛機座椅的坐墊、血壓計的壓脈帶和手術衣，都用得到它。最令人驚嘆的是，它甚至幫忙固定了第一顆人工心臟。

title: 俄羅斯飲酒習慣的由來（How Russia Took to Drinking）

options.C: Today, vodka is still widely known, both in Russia and abroad, as the country’s national drink.
options.D: For many centuries, strong liquor played only a small part in Russian daily life.
options.E: In those days, people in other parts of Europe were far better known for heavy drinking.

optionsZh.A: 沒過多久，伏特加就成了日常飲品，連最窮的人家也不例外。
optionsZh.B: 儘管有種種新政策和運動，酗酒的問題始終沒有從俄羅斯社會消失。

paraLabels: 破題：批評的人認為俄羅斯人天生愛喝酒，但事情沒有這麼簡單
反證一：烈酒很晚才傳進俄羅斯，伏特加也不是本地發明
反證二：15、16 世紀的記載互相矛盾，當時以愛喝酒出名的是歐洲其他地方的人，例如德國人
原因：國家靠伏特加賺錢，價格大跌以後，伏特加成了日常飲品
結尾：禁酒運動持續多年，酗酒的問題到今天仍然存在
marks: Records from the 15th and 16th centuries give contradictory information about how much Russians drank.
The Russian state played a significant role in the spread of drinking.
Meanwhile, a powerful anti-alcohol movement started in the 19th century.
paras: Russia is widely portrayed as the most alcohol-dependent country in the world. Critics of the country say that drinking is almost an inherent trait of the Russian people. However, there is more to the story.

__31__ Before Russia adopted Christianity in the 10th century, people drank mostly beverages with low alcohol content. Vodka, Russia’s national drink, was not a Russian invention. It began as a strong grape spirit that visitors from Genoa, Italy, brought to Moscow in the late 14th century. Russian monks later learned to make their own version of the drink.

Records from the 15th and 16th centuries give contradictory information about how much Russians drank. Some documents noted that Russians “indulge in excessive drinking whenever the occasion arises,” while others claimed that Russians “rarely drink wine.” __32__ There were many sayings about their love of alcohol, such as “drunk as a German.”

The Russian state played a significant role in the spread of drinking. For hundreds of years, the government controlled the vodka trade and collected huge revenues from it. With so much money at stake, Russia’s rulers had every reason to keep people drinking. In the 1860s, changes in government policy caused vodka prices to drop sharply. __33__

Meanwhile, a powerful anti-alcohol movement started in the 19th century. Government policies were introduced and public organizations were set up to prevent the spread of alcoholism. __34__ Although Russia does not rank first in alcohol consumption per person, it is still among the heaviest-drinking countries in the world.
zhTranslation: 一般人常把俄羅斯說成全世界最依賴酒精的國家，批評俄羅斯的人更說，愛喝酒幾乎是俄羅斯人與生俱來的特質。不過，事情沒有這麼簡單。
__31__ 俄羅斯在 10 世紀接受基督教之前，人們喝的大多是酒精濃度低的飲料。至於俄羅斯的國酒伏特加，其實也不是俄羅斯人發明的。它原本是用葡萄蒸餾的烈酒，14 世紀末由來自義大利熱那亞的訪客帶到莫斯科，後來俄羅斯的修士才學會自己製作這種酒。
關於 15、16 世紀的俄羅斯人喝多少酒，當時的記載說法互相矛盾。有的文獻說俄羅斯人「一有機會就喝得過量」，有的卻說俄羅斯人「很少喝葡萄酒」。__32__ 當時有許多俗語形容他們嗜酒，例如「醉得像個德國人」。
喝酒的風氣在俄羅斯越來越普遍，國家在這當中扮演了重要的角色。好幾百年來，政府一直掌控伏特加的買賣，從中賺進龐大的收入。既然牽涉這麼多錢，統治者當然樂於讓人民繼續喝酒。到了 1860 年代，政府政策的改變又讓伏特加的價格大幅下跌。__33__
同一時期，19 世紀也興起一股強大的禁酒運動：政府制定政策，民間也成立團體，要防止酗酒的風氣蔓延。__34__ 雖然以每人平均飲酒量來說，俄羅斯並不是第一名，但仍然是全世界最會喝酒的國家之一。

title: 泰武國小古謠傳唱隊（Young Voices, Ancient Songs）

optionsZh.C: 他真正的目的，是幫助孩子們明白自己為什麼要唱，並且讓文化延續下去。

rows.want: 一句概括傳唱隊在台灣以外受到的肯定，後面的歐洲巡演、日本節目票選才是它的細節

rows.want: 一句概括古謠讓孩子和父母重新認識自己的文化，後面長老、家長、孩子的細節才有主題句
rows.why: E 沒有提到父母，也沒有提到文化

rows.want: 一句說出 Camake 成立傳唱隊真正的用意，和前一句的「國際名聲」相對
rows.why: E 不是任何人的用意，和下一段「把文化帶著走」也沒有關係

paraLabels: 破題：泰武古謠傳唱隊是誰，在國外得到哪些肯定
第一次到歐洲：擔心觀眾睡著，觀眾卻聽得全神貫注
回到部落：孩子唱古謠，父母跟著重新認識自己的文化
初衷：成立傳唱隊不是為了名聲，而是為了讓文化延續
遷村之後：森林和房子帶不走，文化帶得走
marks: Recalling the group’s first tour of Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the group’s founder, admitted that he had felt very nervous.
Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses with us, but we were able to bring our culture along.”
paras: The Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers are a group of Paiwan children from a small school in Pingtung, southern Taiwan. __31__ In 2009, they were invited to perform in several European countries, including Belgium, France, and Germany. Two years later, viewers of the Japanese TV program “Amazing Voice” voted them one of the world’s top five performance groups.

Recalling the group’s first tour of Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the group’s founder, admitted that he had felt very nervous. Most of the 75-minute show was sung a cappella, that is, without any instruments, so he had worried that the audience would fall asleep. __32__ Afterward, people told him that the performance let them picture the children’s village without ever having visited it. The experience greatly boosted the group’s confidence.

__33__ It used to be that only tribal elders in their fifties and sixties could sing these songs. Now that the children perform them, many parents have begun to ask why they themselves never learned the ballads. Often it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, piecing together a memory that had begun to fade.
Winning international fame, however, was never what Camake had in mind when he started the group. __34__

After Typhoon Morakot struck in August 2009, Taiwu Village and its school had to move down from the mountains. Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses with us, but we were able to bring our culture along.” He promised to keep singing with the children for as long as they were willing to sing.
zhTranslation: 泰武國小古謠傳唱隊是一群排灣族的孩子，來自台灣南部屏東的一所小學。__31__ 2009 年，他們受邀到幾個歐洲國家演出，包括比利時、法國和德國。兩年後，日本電視節目《Amazing Voice》的觀眾把他們票選為全球五大表演團體之一。
回想起傳唱隊第一次到歐洲巡迴演出，體育老師、也是傳唱隊創辦人的 Camake Valaule 坦承，他當時非常緊張。75 分鐘的演出大部分是 a cappella，也就是完全沒有樂器伴奏的清唱，所以他一直擔心觀眾會睡著。__32__ 演出結束後，觀眾告訴他，這場演出讓他們不必親自造訪，就能想像出孩子們的村子是什麼模樣。這次經驗讓傳唱隊的信心大增。
__33__ 以前會唱這些歌的，只有五、六十歲的部落長老。現在孩子們唱這些歌，許多家長開始問，為什麼自己從來沒學過這些古謠。如今常常是孩子教父母唱，把漸漸淡去的記憶一點一點拼回來。
不過，Camake 當初成立傳唱隊，心裡想的從來不是贏得國際名聲。__34__
2009 年 8 月莫拉克颱風過後，泰武村和泰武國小不得不從山上遷到山下。Camake 說：「我們帶不走森林，也帶不走我們的房子，但是我們可以把文化帶著走。」他也承諾，只要孩子們願意唱，他就會一直陪著他們唱下去。

title: 研究快樂這件事（The Science of Happiness）

options.A: Studies show that doing kind things for friends and strangers alike tends to make people happier.
options.B: It is hard to know whether one person’s sense of well-being is greater than another’s.
options.C: In a growing field called positive psychology, researchers are looking for ways to make people happier.
options.D: Many people assume that earning more money is the surest way to become happier.
options.E: Researchers can now keep track of how often people genuinely smile in daily life.

optionsZh.A: 研究顯示，不論對朋友還是陌生人，做好事往往能讓人更快樂。
optionsZh.B: 很難知道一個人的幸福感是不是比另一個人的高。
optionsZh.C: 在正向心理學這個日漸成長的領域裡，研究人員正在尋找讓人更快樂的方法。
optionsZh.D: 很多人以為，賺更多錢是讓自己更快樂最可靠的途徑。
optionsZh.E: 研究人員現在可以記錄人們在日常生活中真心微笑的次數。

unusedExplanation.lead: D 這一句文法正確，講的也是怎麼讓人更快樂，和全篇同一個主題；它的 `become happier`（變得更快樂）也和第四段的 `happiness boosters`（能提升快樂的方法）字面相近，最容易被放進第 34 格。可是全篇談的是**心理學家怎麼用科學方法研究快樂、研究出了什麼**，D 說的卻是一般人對金錢的看法，既不是研究，也不是研究的發現。把 D 放進四個空格，每一格都放不下：

rows.want: 一句說出現在的研究人員在哪個領域、想做什麼，和前面「過去只幫助心理疾病患者」形成對比；第二段用 `However`（不過）轉到這類研究的困難，前面也要先有研究的目標
rows.why: D 說的是一般人的想法，不是研究人員在做的事，也和「過去只幫助病人」形成不了對比

rows.want: 一句說出第二個障礙：人和人之間很難比較，後一句我的「8」和你的「6」才是它的例子
rows.why: 第二段講的是測量快樂有哪些困難，D 談金錢和快樂的關係，和「我的 8 分是不是比你的 6 分快樂」接不上

rows.want: 一句說出一種具體的測量做法，後面談真笑和假笑的分別才有來由
rows.why: D 不是測量快樂的方法，後一句突然講起笑容就沒有來由

rows.want: 一句報告第一項研究發現：做什麼事能讓人更快樂，後一句的 `Other research-backed happiness boosters`（其他有研究支持、能提升快樂的方法）才說得通
rows.why: D 只是很多人的看法，沒有研究支持；後一句說「其他有研究支持的」方法，前面要先有一項研究發現

unusedExplanation.summary: **全篇問的是「科學家怎麼研究快樂、研究出了什麼」，D 說的卻是「很多人以為錢能買到快樂」。**這一篇多出來的 D 屬於「主題相同，切面不對」，和 115 學測多出來的 D 同一類。至於 115 學測參考試卷多出來的 C，則屬於「切面對，卻沒有段落在等它」，和這一篇不同。
unusedExplanation.takeaway: 多出來的選項常常和某一段用了相近的字（這一篇是 D 的 happier 和第四段的 happiness boosters），讀起來好像接得上。遇到這種選項，先問它說的是不是這篇文章在談的事情：這一篇每一段都在談研究，一句只講一般人想法的話，就算字面相近，也放不進任何一格。

paraLabels: 引言：心理學家過去只研究心理疾病，如今正向心理學開始研究怎麼讓人更快樂
難題：快樂很難用科學方法測量，人和人之間也很難比較
突破：研究人員找到比較好的測量方法，例如觀察真心的笑容
發現：做好事能讓人更快樂，另有幾種習慣也有研究支持
marks: But today, happiness is a hot subject of research.
However, this kind of research faces significant obstacles.
In recent years, however, researchers have found better ways to measure happiness.
paras: Not long ago, joy wasn’t considered serious enough for psychologists to study. These scientists traditionally helped people with depression or other mental illnesses, not those who were already doing well. But today, happiness is a hot subject of research. __31__

However, this kind of research faces significant obstacles. For one thing, it is difficult to measure a feeling like happiness scientifically. Suppose your best friend says she feels great but is crying a lot and acting more depressed than usual. For the purposes of a scientific study, would you rate her as happy or sad? __32__ On a scale of 1 to 10, how can we be sure that my “8” is happier than your “6”?

In recent years, however, researchers have found better ways to measure happiness. __33__ Real smiles usually look quite different from the forced ones people put on for photographs. A real smile tends to reach the eyes and make the skin around them crinkle, while a fake one often moves only the mouth.

__34__ Other research-backed happiness boosters include keeping a diary of your future dreams, setting and pursuing goals, making friends and family members a big part of your life, expressing optimism about your future, extending gratitude to people who help you, and exercising regularly. The good news is that most of these habits cost little or nothing, so almost anyone can start practicing them today.
zhTranslation: 不久之前，心理學家還認為快樂不夠嚴肅，不值得研究。這些科學家向來幫助的是患有憂鬱症或其他心理疾病的人，而不是本來就過得很好的人。但是現在，快樂成了熱門的研究主題。__31__
不過，這類研究面臨一些重大的障礙。首先，像快樂這樣的感受，很難用科學方法測量。假設你最好的朋友說她感覺很好，卻常常哭，看起來也比平常沮喪；如果是為了做科學研究，你會把她評為快樂還是難過？__32__ 在 1 到 10 分的量表上，我們怎麼能確定我的「8」比你的「6」快樂？
不過，近年來研究人員已經找到比較好的方法來測量快樂。__33__ 真心的笑容和人們拍照時擠出來的笑容，通常看起來很不一樣。真心的笑容往往會牽動眼睛，讓眼睛周圍的皮膚皺起來；假笑則常常只動到嘴巴。
__34__ 其他有研究支持、能提升快樂的方法還包括：把對未來的夢想寫成日記、設定並追求目標、讓親友在生活中占重要的位置、對未來抱持樂觀、向幫助過你的人表達感謝，以及規律運動。好消息是，這些習慣大多不花什麼錢，幾乎每個人今天就可以開始做。

title: 卡內基：從送信童到慈善家（Andrew Carnegie: From Messenger Boy to Philanthropist）

options.A: To keep costs down, he bought the iron mines and railroads that served his steel mills.
options.B: Though he worked long hours, he still found his own ways to keep learning.
options.C: He did not want simply to hand out money; he wanted to help people help themselves.
options.D: In 1901, at the age of 65, he finally sold his company and left business behind.
options.E: In the 1860s, Carnegie saw that the growing railroads would need far more iron.

optionsZh.A: 為了壓低成本，他買下了供應鋼廠原料的鐵礦，以及替鋼廠運貨的鐵路。
optionsZh.B: 雖然工作時間很長，他還是找到了自己的方法繼續學習。
optionsZh.C: 他不想只是把錢送給別人，而是要幫助別人自助。
optionsZh.D: 1901 年，65 歲的他終於賣掉公司，離開了商場。
optionsZh.E: 1860 年代，卡內基看出鐵路越蓋越多，需要的鐵也會大幅增加。

paraLabels: 出身：蘇格蘭織布工之子，手工織布業沒落後，全家移民美國
少年：一到美國就去工作，但工作之餘看戲、借書，繼續學習
事業：看出鐵路需要大量的鐵，改建鐵橋致富，再轉向鋼鐵業
轉折：對商人生活感到不安，想多讀書，1901 年賣掉公司
捐獻：不只是發錢，而是幫助別人自助，捐建 2,500 多座圖書館
marks: Andrew Carnegie, one of the richest men of his time, was born in 1835 to a weaver’s family in Scotland.
However, Carnegie often said he felt uneasy about the life of a businessman.
For the rest of his life, Carnegie devoted himself to giving away his fortune.
paras: Andrew Carnegie, one of the richest men of his time, was born in 1835 to a weaver’s family in Scotland. As a child, he was expected to follow his father’s trade. But when factory machines put hand weavers like his father out of work, the family had to leave for a new life in America.

In 1848, the Carnegies settled near Pittsburgh, then a busy industrial city. Andrew went to work at once, first in a cotton factory and later as a messenger boy in a telegraph office. __31__ When he delivered messages to the city theater, he often stayed to watch plays, especially Shakespeare’s. On Saturday nights, he borrowed books from a small library that a generous local man had opened to working boys.

__32__ Many railroad bridges were still made of wood, which could easily catch fire. He started a company to replace them with stronger iron bridges, and it made him rich. Later, he turned to steel, using a new method from Britain to make it cheaply and in large amounts. By 1900, his mills alone produced more steel than all of Great Britain.

However, Carnegie often said he felt uneasy about the life of a businessman. In a note to himself in 1868, he warned that a life spent chasing more and more money would harm him beyond repair. He wished instead to spend more time studying and reading widely. __33__

For the rest of his life, Carnegie devoted himself to giving away his fortune. He believed that a man who dies rich “dies disgraced.” __34__ Remembering the small library of his boyhood, he paid to build more than 2,500 libraries around the world. By the time he died in 1919, he had given away about $350 million.
zhTranslation: 安德魯·卡內基是當時數一數二的富豪，1835 年出生在蘇格蘭一個織布工的家庭。小時候，家人期待他繼承父親的行業。但是工廠裡的機器讓他父親這樣的手工織布工丟了工作，全家只好前往美國，展開新的生活。
1848 年，卡內基一家在匹茲堡附近落腳，那裡當時是個繁忙的工業城市。安德魯馬上就去工作，先在一家棉紡廠，後來在電報局當送信童。__31__ 他把電報送到市立劇院的時候，常常留下來看戲，尤其是莎士比亞的戲。每到星期六晚上，他就到一間小圖書館借書，那是當地一位熱心人士開放給做工的少年使用的。
__32__ 當時許多鐵路橋還是木造的，很容易起火。他成立一家公司，用更堅固的鐵橋取代這些木橋，因此致富。後來他轉向鋼鐵業，用一種從英國引進的新方法，便宜又大量地煉鋼。到了 1900 年，光是他的鋼廠，產量就超過全英國。
然而，卡內基常常說，他對商人的生活感到不安。1868 年，他寫了一段話提醒自己：一輩子追著越來越多的錢跑，會讓他受到無法挽回的傷害。他反而希望多花點時間求學，廣泛閱讀。__33__
在往後的日子裡，卡內基全心全意地捐出自己的財富。他認為一個人死的時候還很富有，就是「死得可恥」。__34__ 他沒有忘記少年時代那間小圖書館，出錢在世界各地蓋了 2,500 多座圖書館。到 1919 年過世的時候，他一共捐出了大約 3.5 億美元。

title: 非洲學校走向數位化（Schools in Africa Going Digital）

options.A: The country’s state schools, already short of teachers and money, could not handle so many children.
options.B: The prospect of millions of African pupils learning digitally has caught the attention of technology giants.
options.C: Across Africa, far more people own a mobile phone than a computer or tablet.
options.D: If the optimists are right, tablets may soon be as common in African classrooms as blackboards.
options.E: A bigger question is whether tablets and other digital tools actually help children learn.

optionsZh.A: 這個國家的公立學校原本就缺老師、缺經費，應付不了這麼多孩子。
optionsZh.B: 非洲數以百萬計的學生用數位方式學習，這樣的前景引起了科技大廠的注意。
optionsZh.C: 在整個非洲，擁有手機的人遠比擁有電腦或平板的人多。
optionsZh.D: 如果這些樂觀的人看得沒錯，平板在非洲的教室裡可能很快就會和黑板一樣普遍。
optionsZh.E: 更重要的問題是，平板和其他數位工具是不是真的能幫助孩子學習。

unusedExplanation.lead: C 讀起來很順，談的也是非洲的數位裝置：`mobile phone`（手機）和第二段 M-Pesa 用手機轉帳、第四段奈及利亞用手機提供考試工具是同一個字，`tablet`（平板）更是全篇一再出現；說法本身也沒有錯，非洲擁有手機的人確實遠比擁有電腦的人多。問題是，**全篇談的是「非洲的學校走向數位化：為什麼正是時候、誰在投入、到底有沒有效果」，C 說的卻是「一般人擁有哪一種裝置」。**所以四個空格都放不下：

rows.want: 把企業界的樂觀預測落實到教室，說出非洲的學校會有什麼改變，第三段開頭的 `Such a change`（這樣的改變）才有具體的內容
rows.why: C 說的是一般人擁有哪一種裝置，這是現況，不是學校會有的改變；C 也沒有談到學校，第三段說「對肯亞的學校來說正是時候」就沒有著落

rows.want: 說出公立學校應付不了湧進來的大量學生，後面班級人數暴增、物資不夠用才是它的細節
rows.why: C 講的是一般人擁有的裝置，和學生湧入、班級人數暴增都沒有關係

rows.want: 一句概括後面 Amazon、Intel 各項動作的主題句，說出大企業注意到非洲的數位教育
rows.why: 後面三句說的是企業做了什麼，C 說的卻是一般民眾擁有什麼，也概括不了 Kindle 銷量成長十倍這件事

rows.want: 一句提出「數位工具能不能幫助學習」的問題，後面的「初步跡象顯示它們確實有幫助」和三個例子才有回答的對象
rows.why: C 沒有提出任何問題，後面三個學習成效的例子也不是在說明手機比電腦普遍

unusedExplanation.summary: **這一篇談的是非洲的學校怎麼走向數位化：為什麼正是時候、誰在投入、到底有沒有效果；C 談的卻是非洲的一般人擁有哪一種裝置。**這一篇多出來的 C 屬於「主題相同，切面不對」，和 115 學測多出來的 D 同一類。至於 115 學測參考試卷多出來的 C，則屬於「切面對，卻沒有段落在等它」，和這一篇不同。
unusedExplanation.takeaway: 先把四格各自在等什麼寫成一句話，四格都填完再看剩下的那一個。剩下的那一句如果和文章共用幾個字（這一篇是 `mobile phone`、`tablet`），談的卻是文章沒有要談的方向，就可以確定它是多出來的。

paraLabels: 案例：奈洛比 Amaf 學校的學生第一次用平板，上課從黑板、破舊課本換成平板
預測：這是新創公司的試辦計畫，企業界看好數位教育在非洲蓬勃發展，平板可能和黑板一樣普遍
時機：肯亞實施國小免費教育，大批學生湧入，原本就缺老師、缺經費的公立學校應付不來
商機：非洲學生數位學習的前景吸引科技大廠，Amazon、Intel 紛紛投入
成效：更重要的是數位工具能不能幫助學習，初步跡象顯示確實有幫助
marks: Many firms are betting on a boom in digital education in Kenya and elsewhere in Africa.
Such a change would come at just the right time for Kenya’s schools.
paras: Grace Wambui, a 14-year-old pupil in Nairobi, had never touched a tablet computer. But when tablets arrived at Amaf School in Kawangware, a low-income area of the Kenyan capital, it took her only about a minute to work out how to use one. Lessons there used to rely on a blackboard and a handful of worn-out textbooks. Now children in groups of five take turns swiping the touch screens of tablets loaded with a multimedia version of Kenya’s school curriculum.

The tablets at Amaf School are part of a pilot project run by eLimu, a Kenyan technology start-up. Many firms are betting on a boom in digital education in Kenya and elsewhere in Africa. Some business leaders even expect it to take off like M-Pesa, the hugely successful service that lets Kenyans send money by mobile phone. __31__

Such a change would come at just the right time for Kenya’s schools. When Kenya made primary education free in 2003, about 1.3 million extra pupils poured into its classrooms. __32__ At many schools, class sizes soared, some doubling almost overnight. Books, desks, and even pencils ran short.

__33__ Amazon has reported that sales of its Kindle e-readers in Africa grew tenfold in a single year. Intel has been helping African governments buy low-cost computers. In Nigeria, the firm brought together a local publisher and a mobile phone company to offer exam-preparation tools by phone, a service that soon became very popular.

__34__ The early signs suggest that they do. In Ghana, children who were given e-readers by a charity made measurable gains in reading. In Ethiopia, children with no teachers worked out on their own how to use tablets and learned the English alphabet. At Amaf School, average marks in science rose from 58 to 73 in a single term.
zhTranslation: Grace Wambui 是奈洛比一名 14 歲的學生，從來沒有摸過平板電腦。但是平板電腦送到 Amaf 學校的時候，她只花了一分鐘左右，就學會怎麼使用；這所學校位在肯亞首都的低收入地區 Kawangware。以前上課只靠一塊黑板和幾本破舊的課本，現在孩子們五個人一組，輪流滑動平板的觸控螢幕，平板裡裝的是多媒體版本的肯亞課程。
Amaf 學校的平板電腦，是肯亞科技新創公司 eLimu 主持的試辦計畫的一部分。許多公司都看好數位教育會在肯亞和非洲其他地方蓬勃發展，有些企業主管甚至預期，數位教育會像 M-Pesa 一樣一飛沖天；M-Pesa 讓肯亞人用手機就能轉帳，是非常成功的服務。__31__
這樣的改變，對肯亞的學校來說正是時候。肯亞在 2003 年實施國小免費教育，大約 130 萬名新學生湧進教室。__32__ 許多學校的班級人數暴增，有的幾乎一夕之間就多了一倍；書本、桌椅，甚至連鉛筆都不夠用。
__33__ Amazon 表示，旗下 Kindle 電子書閱讀器在非洲的銷量，一年之內成長了十倍。Intel 一直在協助非洲各國政府購買平價電腦；在奈及利亞，Intel 還找來當地一家出版社和一家電信業者合作，用手機提供準備考試的工具，這項服務很快就大受歡迎。
__34__ 初步的跡象顯示，它們確實有幫助。在迦納，一個慈善團體送給孩子電子書閱讀器，這些孩子的閱讀能力有了明顯的進步。在衣索比亞，沒有老師教的孩子自己摸索出平板的用法，還學會了英文字母。在 Amaf 學校，科學的平均分數在一個學期內從 58 分提高到 73 分。

title: 斯巴達松超級馬拉松的魅力（The Allure of the Spartathlon Ultra-Marathon）

options.A: Runners are drawn to the Spartathlon by two things: its difficulty and its history.
options.B: To many finishers, the simple wreath and water mean more than any medal.
options.C: Many runners are also moved by the thought of following in Pheidippides’s footsteps.
options.D: Within just a few minutes, their sore joints and muscles start to stiffen.
options.E: It is recorded that he reached Sparta on the day after he left Athens.

optionsZh.A: 吸引跑者參加斯巴達松的有兩件事情：它的難度和它的歷史。
optionsZh.B: 對許多完賽的跑者來說，簡單的花環和水比任何獎牌都更有意義。
optionsZh.C: 許多跑者也因為想到能循著 Pheidippides 的腳步前進而深受感動。
optionsZh.D: 才短短幾分鐘，他們痠痛的關節和肌肉就開始僵硬。
optionsZh.E: 根據記載，他離開雅典的隔天就抵達了斯巴達。

unusedExplanation.lead: B 讀起來很通順，也沒有離開主題：它講的是跑者完賽時拿到的花環和水。放進第 34 格，`wreath`（花環）、`water`（水）都是第四段第一句出現過的字，乍看像是順著往下說。但四個空格都放不下：

rows.want: 交代 Pheidippides 花了多少時間到斯巴達，後一句 Foden 懷疑有沒有人能「這麼快」跑完才有來由
rows.why: B 講的是今天的完賽場面，和古代的記載無關

rows.want: 總說第三段要談的吸引力，後面列出的各種考驗才有所歸屬
rows.why: B 只談終點的花環和水，概括不了酷熱、低溫、半夜翻山、時間壓力這些考驗

rows.want: 在難度之外補上另一個吸引跑者的原因，而且照應第二段的歷史
rows.why: 花環和水要到第四段完賽時才出現，B 的 `the simple wreath and water`（那簡單的花環和水）在這裡指不到東西；B 也沒有說到歷史，段首說的兩件事情就只講了難度

rows.want: 說出喜悅為什麼很快就消失，後一句跑者在鎮上慢慢走、每一步都很痛才有原因
rows.why: B 回頭肯定完賽那一刻的意義，方向和前一句 `However, the joy does not last long.` 正好相反

unusedExplanation.summary: **B 談的是完賽時的花環和水有什麼意義，它最適合放的位置是第四段第一句後面，可是那裡沒有空格。**這一篇多出來的 B 屬於「切面對，卻沒有段落在等它」，和 115 學測參考試卷多出來的 C 同一類。至於 115 學測多出來的 D，則屬於「主題相同，切面不對」，和這一篇不同。第四段的話題確實是完賽，可是第四段的空格要的是喜悅為什麼消失，不是完賽有什麼意義；B 和空格附近共用的字又多，所以比 115 學測多出來的 D 難認。
unusedExplanation.takeaway: 選項裡出現空格附近的字（像這一篇的 `wreath`、`water`），先別急著填。先遮住選項，想想那個位置需要一句什麼樣的話，再看選項說的是不是那件事。

paraLabels: 引言：斯巴達松是什麼，36 小時內從雅典跑到斯巴達
由來：從 Pheidippides 的記載，到 1982 年 Foden 等人親身驗證，隔年辦成比賽
魅力：吸引跑者的兩件事情，先談難度（各種考驗），再談歷史
完賽之後：喜悅很快消失、身體僵硬，沒過多久卻又想再跑
marks: In the Spartathlon, one of the world’s toughest ultra-marathons, runners cover 246 kilometers, almost six marathons, within 36 hours.
The race’s roots go back to 490 B.C., when an Athenian named Pheidippides made the journey to Sparta to ask the Spartans for help against the invading Persians.
paras: In the Spartathlon, one of the world’s toughest ultra-marathons, runners cover 246 kilometers, almost six marathons, within 36 hours. The runners start in Athens and run all the way to the historic city of Sparta.

The race’s roots go back to 490 B.C., when an Athenian named Pheidippides made the journey to Sparta to ask the Spartans for help against the invading Persians. __31__ In 1982, this story sparked the interest of John Foden, a British air-force officer and long-distance runner, who wondered if anyone could really cover that distance so quickly. Foden and four other runners from the air force decided to see for themselves. Three of the five made it to Sparti, as the town is now called, in less than 40 hours. Their success led to the first Spartathlon a year later.

__32__ The Spartathlon is not the hardest race in the world, but it combines many different tests. There is the heat of the Greek day, and then the sharp drop in temperature when darkness falls. There are long climbs, and in the middle of the night, runners must cross a mountain about 1,200 meters high. Above all, there is the constant pressure of the clock. __33__

As finishers receive a wreath and water from schoolgirls, many are overjoyed. However, the joy does not last long. __34__ After the race, Sparti looks like the set of a zombie movie, as runners move slowly and painfully around the town. But the urge to do it all over again soon appears.
zhTranslation: 斯巴達松（Spartathlon）是世界上最艱難的超級馬拉松之一，跑者要在 36 小時內跑完 246 公里，將近六場馬拉松的距離。跑者從雅典出發，一路跑到歷史悠久的斯巴達。

這項比賽的由來，可以追溯到西元前 490 年：當時一位名叫 Pheidippides 的雅典人前往斯巴達，請斯巴達人幫忙抵抗入侵的波斯人。__31__ 1982 年，這個故事引起了英國空軍軍官、長跑選手 John Foden 的興趣，他想知道是不是真的有人能這麼快就跑完這段路。Foden 和另外四位空軍的跑者決定親自試試看。五個人當中，有三個人在 40 小時內抵達了 Sparti，也就是斯巴達現在的名稱。他們的成功，促成了一年後第一屆斯巴達松的舉辦。
__32__ 斯巴達松不是世界上最難的比賽，卻結合了許多不同的考驗。白天有希臘的酷熱，天黑以後氣溫又急遽下降。路上有很長的上坡，跑者還得在半夜翻過一座大約 1,200 公尺高的山。最重要的是，時間的壓力始終都在。__33__
完賽的跑者從女學生手中接過花環和水，許多人欣喜若狂。不過，這份喜悅維持不了多久。__34__ 賽後的 Sparti 看起來就像殭屍電影的片場，跑者在鎮上慢慢地走來走去，每一步都很痛。但是沒過多久，想再跑一次的念頭又冒了出來。

title: 麝香貓咖啡的價格與來歷（The Price and Origin of Kopi Luwak）

options.A: Many people are put off by the idea of coffee that comes from an animal’s droppings.
options.B: To meet the growing demand, many producers now keep civets in small cages.
options.C: The palm civet is a cat-sized animal that lives in trees and feeds mainly on fruit.
options.D: What is harder to explain is why so little of it is produced.
options.E: Wild civets are thought to seek out and eat only the ripest coffee cherries.

optionsZh.A: 很多人一想到咖啡是從動物糞便裡來的，就倒胃口。
optionsZh.B: 為了滿足日益增加的需求，現在很多業者把椰子狸關在小籠子裡飼養。
optionsZh.C: 椰子狸是體型和貓差不多大的動物，住在樹上，主要以水果為食。
optionsZh.D: 比較難解釋的是，這種咖啡為什麼產量這麼少。
optionsZh.E: 一般認為，野生的椰子狸只會挑最成熟的咖啡果實來吃。

paras: Coffee experts are willing to pay large sums of money for high-quality beans. Premium varieties such as Kona and Blue Mountain are known to cost far more than ordinary coffee. Then there is Kopi Luwak (translated as “civet coffee”), one of the most expensive coffees in the world, which can sell for as much as US$80 a cup.

Its high price is easy to understand, since genuine Kopi Luwak is produced only in very small amounts. __31__ The coffee plants themselves are not rare; the beans found in civet droppings are. That’s right—beans picked out of the body waste of the palm civet. Coffee beans do not become Kopi Luwak until they have passed through the animal’s body.

__32__ Found in South and Southeast Asia, it comes out at night and often visits coffee farms to feed on the cherries. It swallows them whole but digests only their soft outer flesh. Farmers then pick the hard beans out of its droppings, wash them, and roast them.

While the beans survive the trip through the animal, they do not come out unchanged. Juices in the civet’s digestive system break down some of the proteins in the beans, which is believed to make the coffee less bitter. Digestion may not be the whole story, however. __33__

Kopi Luwak is said to taste unlike any other coffee, with hints of caramel and an earthy flavor. Its popularity, though, has come at a high price for the civets. __34__ Fed almost nothing but coffee cherries and kept on wire floors, some of them grow thin and develop painful sores. Since they cannot choose their own cherries, the coffee they produce is often of poorer quality, too.
zhTranslation: 咖啡專家願意花大錢買高品質的咖啡豆。可娜、藍山這類高檔品種，價錢都比一般咖啡貴得多。再來還有 Kopi Luwak（譯為「麝香貓咖啡」），這是全世界最貴的咖啡之一，一杯要價可以高達 80 美元。
它的價格這麼高並不難理解，因為真正的麝香貓咖啡產量非常少。__31__ 稀少的不是咖啡樹本身，而是椰子狸糞便裡的咖啡豆。沒錯，就是從椰子狸的排泄物裡挑出來的咖啡豆。咖啡豆要先通過這種動物的身體，才會成為麝香貓咖啡。
__32__ 椰子狸分布在南亞和東南亞，晚上出來活動，常常跑到咖啡園吃咖啡果實。牠把果實整顆吞下去，但只消化外層柔軟的果肉。農民再從牠的糞便裡挑出堅硬的咖啡豆，洗乾淨後拿去烘焙。
咖啡豆雖然完好地通過椰子狸的身體，出來的時候卻已經不是原來的樣子。椰子狸消化系統裡的消化液會分解咖啡豆裡的一部分蛋白質，一般認為這會讓咖啡比較不苦。不過，消化作用可能不是全部的原因。__33__
據說麝香貓咖啡的味道和其他咖啡都不一樣，帶有焦糖的香氣和泥土般的風味。不過，它這麼受歡迎，椰子狸卻付出了很高的代價。__34__ 這些椰子狸幾乎只吃得到咖啡果實，又被養在鐵絲網地板上，有些變得很瘦，身上還長出疼痛的瘡。而且，牠們沒辦法自己挑選果實，產出的咖啡品質往往也比較差。

Strangely, after the Classic Period ended, many of these cities ceased to be centers of importance.

paras: The Maya built a remarkable civilization that covered much of what is now southern Mexico and northern Central America. __31__ Mayan culture took shape in the Preclassic Period, but it reached its highest development in the Classic Period, from about 250 to 900 AD. During this time, Mayan society was one of the most densely populated and culturally active in the world.

Rather than a single empire, Mayan civilization was made up of many separate city-states that shared a common culture. Strangely, after the Classic Period ended, many of these cities ceased to be centers of importance. __32__ Only the cities were lost, swallowed up by the tropical jungle. Not until the last two hundred years or so did travelers and scholars rediscover and study them. One question that interests scholars is why these cities simply disappeared.

__33__ Toward the end of the Classic Period, there was large-scale, continuous warfare among the city-states. The rulers were highly competitive and made fierce war on one another. Overpopulation was probably also to blame. The Mayan population reached as many as 200 people per square kilometer, among the highest densities in the pre-industrial world. __34__

Studies of ancient pollen show that in many areas, very few trees were left. The loss of so many trees damaged the local environment and helped cause a lack of water and, in time, drought. Thus warfare, overpopulation, overuse of resources, and destruction of the environment all appear to be factors in the disappearance of the Mayan cities.
zhTranslation: 馬雅人建立了一個了不起的文明，範圍涵蓋今天墨西哥南部和中美洲北部的大片地區。__31__ 馬雅文化在前古典期逐漸成形，到了古典期（大約西元 250 年到 900 年）才發展到最高峰。在這段期間，馬雅社會是世界上人口最稠密、文化最活躍的社會之一。
馬雅文明不是一個統一的帝國，而是由許多各自獨立、文化相同的城邦組成。奇怪的是，古典期結束以後，其中許多城市就不再是重要的中心了。__32__ 消失的只有城市，它們淹沒在熱帶叢林裡。一直到最近兩百年左右，旅人和學者才重新發現這些城市，開始研究它們。學者感興趣的一個問題，就是這些城市為什麼就這樣消失了。
__33__ 到了古典期末期，城邦之間爆發大規模、持續不斷的戰爭。統治者彼此競爭激烈，互相猛烈攻伐。人口過多可能也是原因。馬雅的人口密度最高達到每平方公里 200 人，在前工業時代的世界裡數一數二。__34__
古代花粉的研究顯示，在許多地區，樹木已經所剩無幾。失去這麼多樹木，破壞了當地的環境，也是造成缺水、後來發生乾旱的原因之一。因此，戰爭、人口過多、資源過度利用和環境破壞，似乎都是馬雅城市消失的因素。
